bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第089卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 89
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 89

sentences.zh: 【晉紀十一】起閼逢閹茂，盡柔兆困敦，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 11] From Qiefeng Yanmao through Rouzhao Kundun; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 11] From Qiefeng Yanmao through Rouzhao Kundun—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 孝愍皇帝下建興二年（

translations.literal: Second year of Jianxing under Emperor Xiaomin (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Jianxing of Emperor Min (

sentences.zh: 甲戌，公元三一四年）

translations.literal: Jiaxu, CE 314)
translations.idiomatic: year Jiaxu, AD 314)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，有如日隕於地；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinwei, there was something like the sun falling to the ground;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day xinwei, something like the sun fell to the ground;

sentences.zh: 又有三日相承，出西方而東行。

translations.literal: Moreover three suns appeared in succession, coming out from the west and moving eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Three suns also appeared in succession, emerging in the west and traveling east.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingchou, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 有流星出牽牛，入紫微，光燭地，墜於平陽北，化為肉，長三十步，廣二十七步。

translations.literal: A meteor emerged from the Ox constellation, entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, its light illuminating the ground; it fell north of Pingyang and turned into flesh, thirty paces long and twenty-seven paces wide.
translations.idiomatic: A meteor shot out from the Ox, entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, and lit the ground; it fell north of Pingyang and turned into a mass of flesh thirty paces long and twenty-seven paces wide.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰惡之，以問公卿。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong loathed it and questioned the high ministers about it.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler Liu Cong took it as an ill omen and asked his high ministers what it meant.

sentences.zh: 陳元達以為：「女寵太盛，亡國之征。」

translations.literal: Chen Yuanda said: "Female favor is too excessive—a sign of a state's perdition."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda said, "Excessive favor toward women is a sign that the state will perish."

sentences.zh: 聰曰：「此陰陽之理，何關人事！」

translations.literal: Cong said: "This is the principle of yin and yang—what has it to do with human affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied, "That is a matter of yin and yang—what does it have to do with human affairs?"

sentences.zh: 聰後劉氏賢明，聰所為不道，劉氏每規正之。

translations.literal: Cong's empress Liu was worthy and wise; when Cong acted against the Way, Liu would each time admonish and correct him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's empress, Lady Liu, was worthy and wise; whenever Cong behaved wickedly, she would admonish and correct him.

sentences.zh: 己丑，劉氏卒，謚曰武宣。

translations.literal: On jichou, Lady Liu died; her posthumous title was Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Lady Liu died; she was given the posthumous name Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 自是嬖寵競進，後宮無序矣。

translations.literal: From this favored consorts vied to advance, and the inner palace had no order.
translations.idiomatic: From then on favored women vied for advancement, and order in the inner palace was lost.

sentences.zh: 聰置丞相等七公；

translations.literal: Cong established seven dukes including the Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Cong created seven grandee ranks including Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 又置輔漢等十六大將軍，各配兵二千，以諸子為之；

translations.literal: he also established sixteen great generals such as Fu-Han, each assigned two thousand troops, with his sons holding these posts;
translations.idiomatic: he also appointed sixteen great generals such as Fu-Han, each with two thousand troops under command, and gave these posts to his sons;

sentences.zh: 又置左右司隸，各領戶二十餘萬，萬戶置一內史；

translations.literal: he also established Left and Right Directors of Retainers, each overseeing more than two hundred thousand households, with one Interior Minister per ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: he also set up Left and Right Directors of Retainers, each supervising more than two hundred thousand households, with one Interior Minister for every ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 單于左右輔，各主六夷十萬落，萬落置一都尉；

translations.literal: Left and Right Assistants to the Chanyu, each governing one hundred thousand camps of the Six Barbarian peoples, with one commandant per ten thousand camps;
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Assistants to the Chanyu, each in charge of one hundred thousand camps of the Six Barbarian peoples, with one commandant appointed for every ten thousand camps;

sentences.zh: 左、右選曹尚書，並典選舉。

translations.literal: Left and Right Directors of Selection, both in charge of appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Directors of Selection, both responsible for appointments.

sentences.zh: 自司隸以下六官，皆位亞僕射。

translations.literal: From the Directors of Retainers downward, the six offices all ranked just below the Vice Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: From the Directors of Retainers on down, all six offices ranked just below the Vice Ministers.

sentences.zh: 以其子粲為丞相、領大將軍、錄尚書事，進封晉王。

translations.literal: He made his son Can Chancellor, Grand General-in-Chief, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and advanced him to Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his son Can Chancellor, Grand General-in-Chief, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and advanced him to Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 江都王延年錄尚書六條事，汝陰王景為太師，王育為太傅，任顗為太保，馬景為大司徒，朱紀為大司空，中山王曜為大司馬。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangdu Yan Nian recorded the six categories of Masters of Writing affairs; Prince of Ruyin Jing was Grand Preceptor; Wang Yu was Grand Tutor; Ren Yi was Grand Protector; Ma Jing was Grand Minister of Agriculture; Zhu Ji was Grand Minister of Works; Prince of Zhongshan Yao was Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangdu Yan Nian recorded the six categories of Masters of Writing business; Prince of Ruyin Jing became Grand Preceptor; Wang Yu Grand Tutor; Ren Yi Grand Protector; Ma Jing Grand Minister of Agriculture; Zhu Ji Grand Minister of Works; and Prince of Zhongshan Yao Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，王子春等及王浚使者至襄國，石勒匿其勁卒、精甲，羸師虛府以示之，北面拜使者而受書。

translations.literal: On renchen, Wang Zichun and others together with Wang Jun's envoy arrived at Xiangguo; Shi Le hid his crack troops and fine armor, showed them weakened soldiers and empty storehouses, bowed facing north to the envoy and received the letter.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen, Wang Zichun and Wang Jun's envoy reached Xiangguo. Shi Le hid his crack troops and fine armor, displayed only weak soldiers and empty storehouses, bowed north toward the envoy, and accepted the letter.

sentences.zh: 浚遺勒麈尾，勒陽不敢執，懸之於壁，朝夕拜之，曰：「我不得見王公，見其所賜，如見公也。」

translations.literal: Jun sent Le a deer-tail fly-whisk; Le pretended he dared not hold it, hung it on the wall, and bowed to it morning and evening, saying: "Though I cannot see the lord, seeing what he bestowed is like seeing the lord himself."
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Le a deer-tail fly-whisk. Le feigned that he dared not hold it, hung it on the wall, and bowed to it morning and evening, saying, "Though I cannot see my lord, to see what he gave is like seeing my lord himself."

sentences.zh: 復遣董肇奉表於浚，期以三月中旬親詣幽州奉上尊號；

translations.literal: He again sent Dong Zhao to present a memorial to Jun, promising to come in person to Youzhou by mid-third month to offer the exalted title;
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Dong Zhao to present a memorial to Jun, promising to come in person to Youzhou by mid-third month to offer him the exalted title;

sentences.zh: 亦修箋於棗嵩，求并州牧、廣平公。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Zao Song seeking the governorship of Bingzhou and the title Duke of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Zao Song asking for the governorship of Bingzhou and the title Duke of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 勒問浚之政事於王子春，子春曰：「幽州去歲大水，人不粒食，浚積粟百萬，不能賑贍，刑政苛酷，賦役殷煩，忠賢內離，夷狄外叛。

translations.literal: Le asked Wang Zichun about Jun's governance; Zichun said: "Last year Youzhou suffered great floods; people had no grain to eat. Jun stored a million piculs of grain but could not relieve and support them. Penal administration was harsh and cruel, taxes and corvée burdens heavy; the worthy and loyal departed within, the barbarians rebelled without.
translations.idiomatic: Le asked Wang Zichun about Jun's governance. Zichun said, "Last year Youzhou suffered devastating floods and people had no grain to eat. Jun had a million piculs of grain in store but would not relieve them. His punishments were harsh, his taxes and corvée burdens crushing; worthy men deserted him within, and the barbarians rebelled without.

sentences.zh: 人皆知其將亡，而浚意氣自若，曾無懼心，方更置立台閣，布列百官，自謂漢高、魏武不足比也。」

translations.literal: Everyone knows he is about to perish, yet Jun is self-assured in spirit and never fearful; he is now further establishing terrace pavilions and arranging the hundred officials, deeming himself not inferior even to Han Gaozu and Wei Wudi."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows he is doomed, yet Jun remains self-assured and unafraid; he is even setting up terrace offices and arranging a full bureaucracy, declaring that even Han Gaozu and Cao Cao cannot compare with him."

sentences.zh: 勒撫幾笑曰：「王彭祖真可擒也。」

translations.literal: Le stroked the armrest and laughed: "Wang Pengzu can truly be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Le stroked the armrest and laughed, "Wang Pengzu can truly be taken."

sentences.zh: 浚使者還薊，具言「石勒形勢寡弱，款誠無二。」

translations.literal: Jun's envoy returned to Ji and reported in full that "Shi Le's forces are few and weak, and his sincere submission is without duplicity."
translations.idiomatic: Jun's envoy returned to Ji and reported at length that "Shi Le's forces are few and weak and his submission wholly sincere."

sentences.zh: 浚大悅，益驕怠，不復設備。

translations.literal: Jun was greatly pleased, grew still more arrogant and negligent, and made no further preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was greatly pleased, grew still more arrogant and negligent, and made no further preparations for defense.

sentences.zh: 楊虎掠漢中吏民以奔成，梁州人張鹹等起兵逐楊難敵。

translations.literal: Yang Hu plundered the officials and people of Hanzhong and fled to Cheng; Zhang Xian of Liangzhou and others raised troops to drive out Yang Nandi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu plundered the officials and people of Hanzhong and fled to Cheng; Zhang Xian of Liangzhou and others raised troops to drive out Yang Nandi.

sentences.zh: 難敵去，鹹以其地歸成，於是漢嘉、涪陵、漢中之地皆為成有。

translations.literal: When Nandi departed, Xian surrendered the territory to Cheng; thus the lands of Hanjia, Fuling, and Hanzhong all came under Cheng's possession.
translations.idiomatic: When Nandi left, Xian surrendered the territory to Cheng, and the regions of Hanjia, Fuling, and Hanzhong all fell to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 成主雄以李鳳為梁州刺史，任回為寧州刺史，李恭為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Cheng ruler Xiong appointed Li Feng Governor of Liangzhou, Ren Hui Governor of Ningzhou, and Li Gong Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng ruler Li Xiong appointed Li Feng Governor of Liangzhou, Ren Hui Governor of Ningzhou, and Li Gong Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 雄虛己好賢，隨才授任；

translations.literal: Xiong humbled himself and loved the worthy, appointing men according to their talents;
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was humble and loved worthy men, appointing people according to their talents;

sentences.zh: 命太傅驤養民於內，李鳳等招懷於外；

translations.literal: he ordered Grand Tutor Xiang to nurture the people within, while Li Feng and others won people over without;
translations.idiomatic: he had Grand Tutor Xiang nurture the people at home while Li Feng and others won people over abroad;

sentences.zh: 刑政寬簡，獄無滯囚；

translations.literal: penal administration was lenient and simple, and prisons held no long-detained prisoners;
translations.idiomatic: penal policy was lenient and simple, and no prisoners languished in jail;

sentences.zh: 興學校，置史官。

translations.literal: he raised schools and established historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: he founded schools and appointed historiographers.

sentences.zh: 其賦民，男丁歲谷三斛，女丁半之，疾病又半之。

translations.literal: In taxing the people, each adult male paid three hu of grain per year; for females, half; for illness, half again.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes on the people were three hu of grain per adult male each year, half that for females, and half again for the sick.

sentences.zh: 戶調絹不過數丈，綿數兩。

translations.literal: Household levies of silk were no more than a few zhang, and of cotton no more than a few liang.
translations.idiomatic: Household levies in silk amounted to no more than a few zhang, and in cotton to no more than a few liang.

sentences.zh: 事少役希，民多富實，新附者皆給復除。

translations.literal: Affairs were few and corvée rare; the people were mostly wealthy and secure; all newly submitted were granted tax and corvée exemptions.
translations.idiomatic: Public business was light and corvée rare; most people were prosperous; and all who newly submitted were granted tax and corvée exemptions.

sentences.zh: 是時天下大亂，而蜀獨無事，年谷屢熟，乃至閭門不閉，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: At this time the empire was in great disorder, yet Shu alone was untroubled; harvests were repeatedly abundant, so that neighborhood gates were left unbarred and lost goods were not picked up on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: While the empire was in chaos, Shu alone was at peace; harvests were repeatedly good, so that people left their gates unbarred and no one picked up lost goods on the roads.

sentences.zh: 漢嘉夷王沖歸、朱提審炤、建寧爨疆皆歸之。

translations.literal: Chong Gui, Yi king of Hanjia; Shen Zhao of Zhuti; and Cuan Jiang of Jianning all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Gui, Yi king of Hanjia; Shen Zhao of Zhuti; and Cuan Jiang of Jianning all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 巴郡嘗告急，雲有晉兵。

translations.literal: Bajun once reported an emergency, saying Jin troops were coming.
translations.idiomatic: Bajun once sent an urgent report that Jin troops were approaching.

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「吾常憂琅邪微弱，遂為石勒所滅，以為耿耿，不圖乃能舉兵，使人欣然。」

translations.literal: Xiong said: "I have long worried that Langye was weak and would be destroyed by Shi Le; this has weighed on my mind. I never expected that they could raise troops—this makes one rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong said, "I have long feared that the house of Langye was too weak and would be destroyed by Shi Le; it has weighed on my mind. I never expected them to be able to take up arms—this is heartening news."

sentences.zh: 然雄朝無儀器，爵位濫溢；

translations.literal: Yet in Xiong's court there were no ritual vessels, and titles and ranks overflowed without limit;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiong's court lacked ritual regalia, and titles and ranks were handed out without restraint;

sentences.zh: 吏無祿秩，取給於民；

translations.literal: officials had no salary grades and took their support from the people;
translations.idiomatic: officials had no fixed salaries and lived off the people;

sentences.zh: 軍無部伍，號令不肅；

translations.literal: the army had no proper formations, and orders were not strictly enforced;
translations.idiomatic: the army had no proper formations, and orders were not strictly enforced;

sentences.zh: 此其所短也。

translations.literal: these were his shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: these were his shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅，以張軌為太尉、涼州牧，封西平郡公；

translations.literal: In the second month, on renyin, Zhang Gui was made Grand Commandant and Governor of Liangzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day renyin, Zhang Gui was appointed Grand Commandant and Governor of Liangzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping;

sentences.zh: 王浚為大司馬、都督幽、冀諸軍事；

translations.literal: Wang Jun was made Grand Marshal and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in You and Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was appointed Grand Marshal and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in You and Ji;

sentences.zh: 荀組為司空、領尚書左僕射兼司隸校尉，行留台事；

translations.literal: Xun Zu was made Minister of Works, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of Retainers, and handled the affairs of the capital left behind;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu was appointed Minister of Works, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of Retainers, and handled affairs of the remnant court at Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 劉琨為大將軍、都督并州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Liu Kun was made Grand General and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun was appointed Grand General and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以張軌老病，拜其子實為副刺史。

translations.literal: Because Zhang Gui was old and ill, the court appointed his son Shi Vice Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang Gui was old and ill, the court appointed his son Shi Vice Governor.

sentences.zh: 石勒纂嚴，將襲王浚，而猶豫未發。

translations.literal: Shi Le marshaled his troops and was about to strike Wang Jun, yet hesitated and did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le marshaled his troops to attack Wang Jun but hesitated and did not march.

sentences.zh: 張賓曰：「夫襲人者，當出其不意。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin said: "One who strikes another must do so where he is not expected.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said, "A surprise attack must catch the enemy off guard.

sentences.zh: 今軍嚴經日而不行，豈非畏劉琨及鮮卑、烏桓為吾後患乎？」

translations.literal: Now the army has been under strict orders for days yet has not moved—is this not because you fear Liu Kun and the Xianbei and Wuhuan as troubles in your rear?"
translations.idiomatic: The army has been under strict orders for days yet has not moved—is it not because you fear Liu Kun and the Xianbei and Wuhuan as a threat to your rear?"

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「然。

translations.literal: Le said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Le said, "That is so.

sentences.zh: 為之奈何？」

translations.literal: What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: What should we do about it?"

sentences.zh: 賓曰：「彼三方智勇無及將軍者，將軍雖遠出，彼必不敢動，且彼未謂將軍便能懸軍千里取幽州也。

translations.literal: Bin said: "In wisdom and courage those three sides cannot match the general. Though the general goes far away, they surely will not dare move; moreover they do not think the general can lead an army a thousand li to take Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "None of those three rivals matches you in wisdom or courage. Though you march far away, they will not dare move; moreover they will not believe you can lead an army a thousand li to seize Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 輕軍往返，不出二旬，藉使彼雖有心，比其謀議出師，吾已還矣。

translations.literal: A light force going and returning will take no more than twenty days; even if they have the intent, by the time they deliberate and send troops out, we will already have returned.
translations.idiomatic: A light force can go and return within twenty days; even if they mean to act, by the time they debate and march out, we will already be back.

sentences.zh: 且劉琨、王浚，雖同名晉臣，實為仇敵。

translations.literal: Moreover Liu Kun and Wang Jun, though both called Jin ministers, are in fact enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Liu Kun and Wang Jun, though both Jin ministers in name, are in fact enemies.

sentences.zh: 若修箋於琨，送質請和，琨必喜我之服而快浚之亡，終不救浚而襲我也。

translations.literal: If you send a letter to Kun and send hostages to seek peace, Kun will surely rejoice at our submission and be pleased at Jun's fall, and in the end will not rescue Jun but attack us.
translations.idiomatic: If you send Kun a letter and hostages seeking peace, he will rejoice at our submission and be glad to see Jun fall; in the end he will not rescue Jun but attack us instead.

sentences.zh: 用兵貴神速，勿後時也。」

translations.literal: In using troops, speed is prized—do not miss the moment."
translations.idiomatic: In war, speed is everything—do not miss the moment."

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「吾所未了，右候已了之，吾復何疑！」

translations.literal: Le said: "What I had not settled, the Right Marquis has already settled—what further doubt have I!"
translations.idiomatic: Le said, "What I had not yet resolved, you have already resolved—what further doubt can I have!"

sentences.zh: 遂以火宵行，至柏人，殺主簿游綸，以其兄統在范陽，恐洩軍謀故也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he marched by torchlight at night, reached Bairen, and killed Registrar You Lun, because Lun's elder brother Tong was at Fanyang and he feared the military plan would be leaked.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched by torchlight at night. Reaching Bairen, he killed Registrar You Lun because Lun's elder brother Tong was at Fanyang and he feared the plan would be disclosed.

sentences.zh: 遣使奉箋送質於劉琨，自陳罪惡，請討浚以自效。

translations.literal: He sent envoys with a letter and hostages to Liu Kun, confessing his crimes and asking to attack Jun to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with a letter and hostages to Liu Kun, confessing his crimes and offering to attack Jun to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 琨大喜，移檄州郡，稱「己與猗盧方議討勒，勒走伏無地，求拔幽都以贖罪。

translations.literal: Kun was greatly pleased and issued a proclamation to the provinces and commanderies, saying: "I am just now discussing with Tuoba Yilu the campaign against Le; Le has nowhere to flee or hide and asks to raise Youzhou to atone for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was greatly pleased and issued a proclamation to the provinces, saying, "I am just now planning with Tuoba Yilu to attack Le; Le has nowhere to hide and asks to seize Youzhou to atone for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 今便當遣六修南襲平陽，除僭偽之逆類，降知死之逋羯。

translations.literal: I shall now send Liuxiu south to strike Pingyang, eliminate the usurping rebel kind, and subdue the fugitive Jie who know they deserve death.
translations.idiomatic: I shall now send Liuxiu south against Pingyang to destroy the usurping rebels and subdue the fugitive Jie who know they are doomed.

sentences.zh: 順天副民，翼奉皇家，斯乃曩年積誠靈祐之所致也！」

translations.literal: Obeying Heaven and assisting the people, supporting the imperial house—this is what years of accumulated sincerity and spiritual blessing have brought about!"
translations.idiomatic: Obeying Heaven, aiding the people, and supporting the imperial house—this is the fruit of years of accumulated sincerity and divine favor!"

sentences.zh: 三月，勒軍達易水，王浚督護孫緯馳遣白浚，將勒兵拒之，游統禁之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Le's army reached the Yi River; Wang Jun's Supervisor Sun Wei urgently sent word to Jun that Le's troops were coming to resist him, but You Tong forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Le's army reached the Yi River. Wang Jun's supervisor Sun Wei urgently reported that Le was advancing to attack, but You Tong forbade any response.

sentences.zh: 浚將佐皆曰：「胡貪而無信，必有詭計，請擊之。」

translations.literal: Jun's generals and aides all said: "The barbarians are greedy and faithless; there must be a stratagem—please strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Jun's generals and aides all said, "The barbarians are greedy and untrustworthy; this must be a trick—please attack them."

sentences.zh: 浚怒曰：「石公來，正欲奉戴我耳；

translations.literal: Jun angrily said: "Lord Shi is coming precisely to install and honor me;
translations.idiomatic: Jun angrily said, "Lord Shi is coming precisely to install me as emperor;

sentences.zh: 敢言擊者斬！」

translations.literal: whoever dares speak of attacking shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: whoever dares speak of attacking shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 眾不敢復言。

translations.literal: The crowd dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak again.

sentences.zh: 浚設饗以待之。

translations.literal: Jun set out a feast to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun prepared a feast to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 壬申，勒晨至薊，叱門者開門；

translations.literal: On renshen, Le arrived at Ji at dawn and shouted for the gatekeepers to open the gates;
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen, Le reached Ji at dawn and ordered the gatekeepers to open the gates;

sentences.zh: 猶疑有伏兵，先驅牛羊數千頭，聲言上禮，實欲塞諸街巷。

translations.literal: still suspecting ambush, he first drove several thousand head of cattle and sheep, claiming they were tribute, but in fact intending to block the streets and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: still fearing ambush, he first drove several thousand cattle and sheep ahead, claiming they were tribute but in fact to block the streets.

sentences.zh: 浚始懼，或坐或起。

translations.literal: Jun began to fear, now sitting, now rising.
translations.idiomatic: Jun began to fear, rising and sitting uneasily.

sentences.zh: 勒既入城，縱兵大掠，浚左右請御之，浚猶不許。

translations.literal: Once Le had entered the city, he let his troops plunder on a great scale; Jun's attendants asked to resist them, but Jun still would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Le entered the city, he let his troops plunder freely. Jun's attendants begged to resist, but Jun still refused.

sentences.zh: 勒升其聽事，浚乃走出堂皇，勒眾執之。

translations.literal: Le ascended to his audience hall; Jun then fled out to the main hall, and Le's troops seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Le ascended to Jun's audience hall. Jun fled to the main hall, and Le's troops seized him.

sentences.zh: 勒召浚妻，與之並坐，執浚立於前。

translations.literal: Le summoned Jun's wife, sat with her side by side, and had Jun held standing before them.
translations.idiomatic: Le summoned Jun's wife, sat beside her, and had Jun held standing before them.

sentences.zh: 浚罵曰：「胡奴調乃公，何凶逆如此！」

translations.literal: Jun cursed: "Barbarian slave, you dare mock your lord—how can you be so vicious and rebellious!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun cursed, "Barbarian slave, you dare mock your lord—how can you be so vicious and rebellious!"

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「公位冠元台，手握強兵，坐觀本朝傾覆，曾不救援，乃欲自尊為天子，非凶逆乎！

translations.literal: Le said: "Your rank crowns the chief terrace, your hand holds a strong army; you sat and watched our dynasty collapse and never rescued it, yet wished to exalt yourself as Son of Heaven—is this not vicious rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Le said, "You held the highest office and commanded a strong army, yet sat by while the dynasty collapsed without lifting a finger, and wished to make yourself emperor—is that not vicious rebellion!

sentences.zh: 又委任奸貪，殘虐百姓，賊害忠良，毒遍燕土，此誰之罪也！」

translations.literal: Moreover you entrusted the wicked and greedy, cruelly abused the people, harmed the loyal and good, and poison spread throughout the land of Yan—whose crime is this!"
translations.idiomatic: You entrusted the wicked and greedy, cruelly abused the people, harmed the loyal, and spread misery throughout Yan—whose fault is that!"

sentences.zh: 使其將王洛生以五百騎先送浚於襄國。

translations.literal: He had his general Wang Luosheng take five hundred horsemen to escort Jun first to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He had his general Wang Luosheng escort Jun to Xiangguo ahead of him with five hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 浚自投於水，束而出之，斬於襄國市。

translations.literal: Jun threw himself into the water; they bound him and pulled him out, and beheaded him in the market at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Jun threw himself into the water; they bound him, pulled him out, and beheaded him in the market at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒殺浚麾下精兵萬人，浚將佐等爭詣軍門謝罪，饋賂交錯；

translations.literal: Le killed ten thousand crack troops under Jun's command; Jun's generals and aides all vied to come to the camp gate to beg pardon, gifts and bribes crossing in profusion;
translations.idiomatic: Le killed ten thousand of Jun's crack troops. Jun's generals and aides all rushed to the camp gate to beg pardon, gifts and bribes flowing in profusion;

sentences.zh: 前尚書裴憲、從事中郎荀綽獨不至，勒召而讓之曰：「王浚暴虐，孤討而誅之，諸人皆來慶謝，二君獨與之同惡，將何以逃其戮乎！」

translations.literal: Former Master of Writing Pei Xian and Attendant Gentleman Xun Chuo alone did not come; Le summoned and reproached them, saying: "Wang Jun was brutal and tyrannical; I campaigned and executed him. All the others came to congratulate and thank me—why do you two alone share his evil? How will you escape execution!"
translations.idiomatic: Former Master of Writing Pei Xian and Attendant Gentleman Xun Chuo alone did not come. Le summoned and rebuked them: "Wang Jun was brutal and tyrannical; I campaigned against him and executed him. Everyone else came to congratulate me—why do you two alone share his guilt? How will you escape death!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「憲等世仕晉朝，荷其榮祿，浚雖凶粗，猶是晉之籓臣，故憲等從之，不敢有貳。

translations.literal: They replied: "Xian and the rest have served the Jin dynasty for generations and received its honors and salaries. Though Jun was fierce and coarse, he was still a Jin feudatory minister; therefore we followed him and dared not be disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We have served the Jin dynasty for generations and received its honors. Though Jun was brutal, he was still a Jin feudatory minister; we followed him and dared not be disloyal.

sentences.zh: 明公苟不修德義，專事威刑，則憲等死自其分，又何逃乎！

translations.literal: If Your Excellency will not cultivate virtue and righteousness but relies solely on severity and punishment, then death is our proper lot—how could we escape!
translations.idiomatic: If you will not cultivate virtue but rely solely on severity and punishment, then death is our proper lot—how could we escape!

sentences.zh: 請就死。」

translations.literal: We ask to accept death."
translations.idiomatic: We ask only to die."

sentences.zh: 不拜而出。

translations.literal: Without bowing they went out.
translations.idiomatic: Without bowing, they went out.

sentences.zh: 勒召而謝之，待以客禮。

translations.literal: Le summoned them back and apologized, treating them with the courtesy due guests.
translations.idiomatic: Le summoned them back and apologized, treating them as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 綽，勖之孫也。

translations.literal: Chuo was the grandson of Xun Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo was the grandson of Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 勒數朱碩、棗嵩等以納賄亂政，為幽州患，責游統以不忠所事，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Le enumerated the crimes of Zhu Shuo, Zao Song, and others for taking bribes and corrupting government, bringing calamity to Youzhou; he blamed You Tong for disloyalty to his master—and all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Le listed the crimes of Zhu Shuo, Zao Song, and others for taking bribes and corrupting government, bringing ruin to Youzhou; he blamed You Tong for disloyalty to his master—and all were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 籍浚將佐、親戚家貲，皆至巨萬，惟裴憲、荀綽止有書百餘帙，鹽米各十餘斛而已。

translations.literal: The household goods of Jun's generals, aides, and kin were inventoried; all reached tens of thousands, but Pei Xian and Xun Chuo had only a little over a hundred scrolls of books and a little over ten hu each of salt and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The property of Jun's generals, aides, and kin was inventoried; all had fortunes in the tens of thousands, but Pei Xian and Xun Chuo had only a little over a hundred scrolls of books and a little over ten hu each of salt and grain.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「吾不喜得幽州，喜得二子。」

translations.literal: Le said: "I am not pleased to have gained Youzhou; I am pleased to have gained these two men."
translations.idiomatic: Le said, "I am not pleased to have gained Youzhou; I am pleased to have gained these two men."

sentences.zh: 以憲為從事中郎，綽為參軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Xian Attendant Gentleman and Chuo Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xian Attendant Gentleman and Chuo Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 分遣流民，各還鄉里。

translations.literal: He dispersed the displaced people, each returning to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the displaced people home, each to his native district.

sentences.zh: 勒停薊二日，焚浚宮殿，以故尚書燕國劉翰行幽州刺史，戍薊，置守宰而還。

translations.literal: Le halted at Ji for two days, burned Jun's palaces, appointed former Master of Writing Liu Han of Yan as Acting Governor of Youzhou, garrisoned Ji, set up guards and magistrates, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Le stayed at Ji two days, burned Jun's palaces, made former Master of Writing Liu Han of Yan acting Governor of Youzhou, left a garrison and local officials at Ji, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 孫緯遮擊之，勒僅而得免。

translations.literal: Sun Wei intercepted and struck him; Le barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wei intercepted and attacked him; Le barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 勒至襄國，遣使奉王浚首獻捷於漢，漢以勒為大都督、督陝東諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、東單于，增封十二郡；

translations.literal: Le reached Xiangguo and sent envoys presenting Wang Jun's head to report victory to Han; Han made Le Grand Commander-in-Chief, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs east of the Pass, General of Agile Cavalry, and Eastern Chanyu, adding twelve commanderies to his fief;
translations.idiomatic: Le reached Xiangguo and sent envoys with Wang Jun's head to report victory to Han. Han appointed Le Grand Commander-in-Chief, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs east of the Pass, General of Agile Cavalry, and Eastern Chanyu, and added twelve commanderies to his fief;

sentences.zh: 勒固辭，受二郡而已。

translations.literal: Le firmly declined and accepted only two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Le firmly declined and accepted only two commanderies.

sentences.zh: 劉琨請兵於拓跋猗盧以擊漢，會猗盧所部雜胡萬餘家謀應石勒，猗盧悉誅之，不果赴琨約。

translations.literal: Liu Kun asked Tuoba Yilu for troops to attack Han; but more than ten thousand households of mixed barbarians under Yilu plotted to join Shi Le, and Yilu executed them all, so he did not fulfill his pact with Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun asked Tuoba Yilu for troops to attack Han, but more than ten thousand households of mixed peoples under Yilu plotted to join Shi Le. Yilu executed them all and failed to honor his pact with Kun.

sentences.zh: 琨知石勒無降意，乃大懼，上表曰：「東北八州，勒滅其七；

translations.literal: Knowing that Shi Le had no intention of submitting, Kun was greatly afraid and submitted a memorial saying: "Of the eight northeastern provinces, Le has destroyed seven;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Shi Le had no intention of submitting, Kun was greatly afraid and submitted a memorial: "Of the eight northeastern provinces, Le has destroyed seven;

sentences.zh: 先朝所授，存者惟臣。

translations.literal: of what the former court granted, only I remain.
translations.idiomatic: of what the former court granted, only I remain.

sentences.zh: 勒據襄國，與臣隔山，朝發夕至，城塢駭懼，雖懷忠憤，力不從願耳！」

translations.literal: Le holds Xiangguo, separated from me only by mountains; he can arrive from morning to evening, and fortresses and walled towns are terrified. Though I harbor loyal indignation, my strength cannot follow my will!"
translations.idiomatic: Le holds Xiangguo, separated from me only by mountains; he can strike from dawn to dusk, and every fortress is terrified. Though I harbor loyal rage, my strength cannot match my will!"

sentences.zh: 劉翰不欲從石勒，乃歸段匹磾，匹磾遂據薊城。

translations.literal: Liu Han did not wish to follow Shi Le and went over to Duan Pidi; Pidi then seized Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Han refused to follow Shi Le and went over to Duan Pidi, who then seized Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 王浚從事中郎陽裕，耽之兄子也，逃奔令支，依段疾陸眷。

translations.literal: Wang Jun's Attendant Gentleman Yang Yu, a nephew of Yang Dan, fled to Lingzhi and attached himself to Duan Jilujuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's Attendant Gentleman Yang Yu, a nephew of Yang Dan, fled to Lingzhi and attached himself to Duan Jilujuan.

sentences.zh: 會稽朱左車、魯國孔纂、泰山胡母翼自薊逃奔昌黎，依慕容廆。

translations.literal: Zhu Zuoche of Kuaiji, Kong Zuan of Lu, and Humu Yi of Taishan fled from Ji to Changli and attached themselves to Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zuoche of Kuaiji, Kong Zuan of Lu, and Humu Yi of Taishan fled from Ji to Changli and attached themselves to Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 是時中國流民歸廆者數萬家，廆以冀州人為冀陽郡，豫州人為成周郡，青州人為營丘郡，并州人為唐國郡。

translations.literal: At this time tens of thousands of refugee households from China submitted to Hui; Hui made a Jiyang Commandery for people from Jizhou, a Chengzou Commandery for people from Yuzhou, a Yingqiu Commandery for people from Qingzhou, and a Tangguo Commandery for people from Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At this time tens of thousands of refugee households from China submitted to Hui. He organized them into Jiyang Commandery for people from Jizhou, Chengzou for Yuzhou, Yingqiu for Qingzhou, and Tangguo for Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，王浚以邵續為樂陵太守，屯厭次。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Jun had appointed Shao Xu Governor of Leling, stationed at Yanci.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Jun had appointed Shao Xu Governor of Leling, stationed at Yanci.

sentences.zh: 浚敗，續附於石勒，勒以續子乂為督護。

translations.literal: When Jun was defeated, Xu submitted to Shi Le, and Le made Xu's son Yi Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was defeated, Xu submitted to Shi Le, who made Xu's son Yi his supervisor.

sentences.zh: 浚所署勃海太守東萊劉胤棄郡依續，謂續曰：「凡立大功，必杖大義。

translations.literal: Liu Yin of Donglai, whom Jun had appointed Governor of Bohai, abandoned his commandery and joined Xu, saying to Xu: "To achieve great merit one must rely on great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin of Donglai, whom Jun had appointed Governor of Bohai, abandoned his commandery and joined Xu, saying, "To achieve great merit one must rely on great righteousness.

sentences.zh: 君，晉之忠臣，奈何從賊以自污乎！」

translations.literal: You are a loyal minister of Jin—how can you follow bandits and defile yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: You are a loyal minister of Jin—how can you follow bandits and defile yourself!"

sentences.zh: 會段匹磾以書邀續同歸左丞相睿，續從之。

translations.literal: When Duan Pidi invited Xu by letter to return together to Left Chancellor Rui, Xu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Pidi invited Xu by letter to return together to Left Chancellor Rui, Xu agreed.

sentences.zh: 其人皆曰：「今棄勒歸匹磾，其如乂何？」

translations.literal: His men all said: "If we now abandon Le and return to Pidi, what will become of Yi?"
translations.idiomatic: His men all said, "If we now abandon Le and return to Pidi, what will become of Yi?"

sentences.zh: 續泣曰：「我豈得顧子而為叛臣哉！」

translations.literal: Xu wept and said: "How could I care for my son and become a rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu wept and said, "How could I care for my son and become a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 殺異議者數人。

translations.literal: He killed several who dissented.
translations.idiomatic: He killed several who dissented.

sentences.zh: 勒聞之，殺乂。

translations.literal: When Le heard of it, he killed Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Le heard of it, he killed Yi.

sentences.zh: 續遣劉胤使江東，睿以胤為參軍，以續為平原太守。

translations.literal: Xu sent Liu Yin as envoy to the lower Yangtze; Rui made Yin Army Aide and Xu Governor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu sent Liu Yin as envoy to the lower Yangtze. Rui made Yin Army Aide and Xu Governor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣兵圍續，匹磾使其弟文鴦救之，勒引去。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent troops to besiege Xu; Pidi had his younger brother Wenying rescue him, and Le withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent troops to besiege Xu. Pidi sent his younger brother Wenying to rescue him, and Le withdrew.

sentences.zh: 襄國大饑，谷二升直銀一斤，肉一斤直銀一兩。

translations.literal: There was great famine in Xiangguo: two sheng of grain cost one jin of silver, and one jin of meat cost one liang of silver.
translations.idiomatic: There was great famine in Xiangguo: two sheng of grain cost one jin of silver, and one jin of meat one liang of silver.

sentences.zh: 杜苾將王真襲陶侃於休障，侃奔灄中。

translations.literal: Du Bi's general Wang Zhen attacked Tao Kan at Xiuzhang; Kan fled to Tanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Bi's general Wang Zhen attacked Tao Kan at Xiuzhang; Kan fled to Tanzhong.

sentences.zh: 周訪救侃，擊苾兵，破之。

translations.literal: Zhou Fang rescued Kan, struck Bi's troops, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang rescued Kan, attacked Bi's troops, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，西平武穆公張軌寢疾，遺令：「文武將佐，務安百姓，上思報國，下以寧家。」

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Zhang Gui, Duke of Xiping, was gravely ill and left instructions: "Civil and military officers must strive to secure the people, think above of serving the state, and below of settling their households."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Zhang Gui, Duke of Xiping, fell gravely ill and left instructions: "Civil and military officers must secure the people, think above of serving the state, and below of settling their households."

sentences.zh: 己丑，軌薨；

translations.literal: On jichou, Gui died;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Gui died;

sentences.zh: 長史張璽等表世子實攝父位。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhang Xi and others memorialized that the heir Shi should act in his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhang Xi and others memorialized that the heir Shi should act in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 漢中山王曜、趙染寇長安。

translations.literal: Han Prince of Zhongshan Yao and Zhao Ran raided Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Han Prince of Zhongshan Yao and Zhao Ran raided Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 六月，曜屯渭汭，染屯新豐，索綝將兵出拒之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yao encamped at the Wei bend, Ran at Xinfeng, and Suo Jin led troops out to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yao encamped at the Wei bend, Ran at Xinfeng, and Suo Jin led troops out to resist them.

sentences.zh: 染有輕綝之色，長史魯徽曰：「晉之君臣，自知強弱不敵，將致死於我，不可輕也。」

translations.literal: Ran had a contemptuous look toward Jin; Chief Clerk Lu Hui said: "The Jin ruler and ministers know they are no match in strength and will fight to the death against us—we must not take them lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Ran looked down on Jin. Chief Clerk Lu Hui said, "The Jin ruler and ministers know they are outmatched and will fight to the death—we must not take them lightly."

sentences.zh: 染曰：「以司馬模之強，吾取之如拉朽；

translations.literal: Ran said: "With the strength of Sima Mo, I took him as easily as pulling rotten wood apart;
translations.idiomatic: Ran said, "With Sima Mo's strength, I took him as easily as pulling rotten wood apart;

sentences.zh: 索綝小豎，豈能污吾馬蹄、刀刃邪！」

translations.literal: Suo Jin is a little fellow—how could he stain my horse's hooves or my blade!"
translations.idiomatic: Suo Jin is a little fellow—how could he stain my horse's hooves or my blade!"

sentences.zh: 晨，帥輕騎數百逆之，曰：「要當獲綝而後食。」

translations.literal: At dawn he led several hundred light horsemen to meet him, saying: "I must capture Jin before I eat."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he led several hundred light horsemen to meet him, saying, "I must capture Jin before I eat."

sentences.zh: 綝與戰於城西，染兵敗而歸，悔曰：「吾不用魯徽之言以至此，何面目見之！」

translations.literal: Jin fought him west of the city; Ran's troops were defeated and he returned, regretting: "I did not heed Lu Hui's words and came to this—what face have I to see him!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin fought him west of the city. Ran was defeated and returned, regretting, "I did not heed Lu Hui's words and came to this—what face have I to see him!"

sentences.zh: 先命斬徽。

translations.literal: He first ordered Hui beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He first ordered Hui beheaded.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「將軍愚愎以取敗，乃復忌前害勝，誅忠良以逞忿，猶有天地，將軍其得死於枕席乎！」

translations.literal: Hui said: "The general was stupid and obstinate and so met defeat, yet now you resent one who foresaw victory, execute the loyal and good to vent your rage—while Heaven still stands, will the general die in his bed!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "You were stupid and obstinate and met defeat, yet now you resent one who foresaw victory and execute the loyal to vent your rage—while Heaven still stands, will you die in your bed!"

sentences.zh: 詔加索綝驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、錄尚書，承製行事。

translations.literal: An edict added to Suo Jin the titles General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with authority to act by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added to Suo Jin the titles General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with authority to act by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 曜、染復與將軍殷凱帥眾數萬向長安，麴允逆戰於馮翊，允敗，收兵；

translations.literal: Yao and Ran again joined General Yin Kai leading tens of thousands toward Chang'an; Qu Yun met them in battle at Fengyi, was defeated, and withdrew his troops;
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Ran again joined General Yin Kai leading tens of thousands toward Chang'an. Qu Yun met them at Fengyi, was defeated, and withdrew;

sentences.zh: 夜，襲凱營，凱敗死。

translations.literal: at night he raided Kai's camp; Kai was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: at night he raided Kai's camp; Kai was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 曜乃還攻河內太守郭默於懷，列三屯圍之。

translations.literal: Yao then returned to attack Guo Mo, Governor of Henei, at Huai, setting up three camps to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao then returned to attack Guo Mo, Governor of Henei, at Huai, setting up three camps to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 默食盡，送妻子為質，請糴於曜；

translations.literal: When Mo's food was exhausted, he sent his wife and children as hostages and asked to buy grain from Yao;
translations.idiomatic: When Mo's food ran out, he sent his wife and children as hostages and asked to buy grain from Yao;

sentences.zh: 糴畢，復嬰城固守。

translations.literal: when the grain was delivered, he again closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: when the grain arrived, he again shut the city and held firm.

sentences.zh: 曜怒，沉默妻子於河而攻之。

translations.literal: Yao was enraged, drowned Mo's wife and children in the river, and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was enraged, drowned Mo's wife and children in the river, and attacked.

sentences.zh: 默欲投李矩於新鄭，矩使其甥郭誦迎之。

translations.literal: Mo wished to go over to Li Ju at Xinzheng; Ju sent his nephew Guo Song to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Mo wished to go over to Li Ju at Xinzheng; Ju sent his nephew Guo Song to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 兵少，不敢進。

translations.literal: Their troops were few and they dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Their troops were few and they dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 會劉琨遣參軍張肇帥鮮卑五百餘騎詣長安，道阻不通，還，過矩營，矩說肇，使擊漢兵。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Liu Kun sent Army Aide Zhang Zhao with more than five hundred Xianbei horsemen toward Chang'an; the road was blocked and they could not pass, so they returned, passed Ju's camp, and Ju persuaded Zhao to strike the Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Kun sent Army Aide Zhang Zhao with more than five hundred Xianbei horsemen toward Chang'an. The road was blocked, so they returned, passed Ju's camp, and Ju persuaded Zhao to attack the Han troops.

sentences.zh: 漢兵望見鮮卑，不戰而走，默遂帥眾歸矩。

translations.literal: The Han troops saw the Xianbei and fled without fighting; Mo then led his followers back to Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The Han troops saw the Xianbei and fled without fighting; Mo then led his followers to Ju.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰召曜還屯蒲板。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong recalled Yao to encamp at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Cong recalled Yao to encamp at Puban.

sentences.zh: 秋，趙染攻北地，麴允拒之，染中弩而死。

translations.literal: In autumn, Zhao Ran attacked Beidi; Qu Yun resisted him, and Ran was hit by a crossbow bolt and died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, Zhao Ran attacked Beidi. Qu Yun resisted him, and Ran was hit by a crossbow bolt and died.

sentences.zh: 石勒始命州郡閱實戶口，戶出帛二匹，谷二斛。

translations.literal: Shi Le first ordered the provinces and commanderies to verify household registers: each household was to provide two bolts of silk and two hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le first ordered the provinces and commanderies to verify household registers: each household was to provide two bolts of silk and two hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以張實為都督涼州諸軍事、涼州刺史、西平公。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Zhang Shi was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Liangzhou, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Zhang Shi was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Liangzhou, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 十一月，漢主聰以晉王粲為相國、大單于，總百揆。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Han ruler Cong made Prince of Jin Can Chancellor and Grand Chanyu, overseeing all government.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Han ruler Cong made Prince of Jin Can Chancellor and Grand Chanyu, overseeing all government.

sentences.zh: 粲少有俊才，自為宰相，驕奢專恣，遠賢親佞，嚴刻愎諫，國人始惡之。

translations.literal: Can had outstanding talent from youth; once he became Chancellor he was arrogant, extravagant, and willful, kept the worthy at a distance and drew the flatterers close, was harsh and obstinate against remonstrance—the people of the state began to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: Can had outstanding talent from youth. Once he became Chancellor he grew arrogant, extravagant, and willful, kept the worthy at a distance and drew flatterers close, and was harsh and obstinate against remonstrance—the people began to hate him.

sentences.zh: 周勰以其父遺言，因吳人之怨，謀作亂；

translations.literal: Zhou Xie, relying on his father's dying words and the resentment of the people of Wu, plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xie, relying on his father's dying words and Wu resentment, plotted rebellion;

sentences.zh: 使吳興功曹徐馥矯稱叔父丞相從事中郎札之命，收合徒眾，以討王導、刁協，豪傑翕然附之，孫皓族人弼亦起兵於廣德以應之。

translations.literal: he had Wu Xing Registrar Xu Fu falsely claim orders from his uncle, Chancellor's Attendant Gentleman Zha, to gather followers and attack Wang Dao and Diao Xie; heroes flocked to join him, and Sun Hao's clansman Bi also raised troops at Guangde in response.
translations.idiomatic: he had Wu Xing Registrar Xu Fu falsely claim orders from his uncle, Chancellor's Attendant Gentleman Zha, to gather followers and attack Wang Dao and Diao Xie. Heroes flocked to him, and Sun Hao's clansman Bi also raised troops at Guangde in response.

sentences.zh: 孝愍皇帝下建興三年（

translations.literal: Third year of Jianxing under Emperor Xiaomin (
translations.idiomatic: Third year of Jianxing of Emperor Min (

sentences.zh: 乙亥，公元三一五年）

translations.literal: Yihai, CE 315)
translations.idiomatic: year Yihai, AD 315)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，徐馥殺吳興太守袁琇，有眾數千，欲奉周札為主。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Xu Fu killed Wu Xing Governor Yuan Xiu and had several thousand followers; he wished to install Zhou Zha as leader.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Xu Fu killed Wu Xing Governor Yuan Xiu and gathered several thousand followers; he wished to install Zhou Zha as leader.

sentences.zh: 札聞之，大驚，以告義興太守孔侃。

translations.literal: When Zha heard of it he was greatly alarmed and told Yixing Governor Kong Kan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zha heard of it he was greatly alarmed and told Yixing Governor Kong Kan.

sentences.zh: 勰知札意不同，不敢發。

translations.literal: Xie knew Zha's mind was not with him and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Xie knew Zha's mind was not with him and did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 馥黨懼，攻馥，殺之；

translations.literal: Fu's faction grew afraid, attacked Fu, and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Fu's faction grew afraid, attacked Fu, and killed him;

sentences.zh: 孫弼亦死。

translations.literal: Sun Bi also died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi also died.

sentences.zh: 札子續亦聚眾應馥，左丞相睿議發兵討之。

translations.literal: Zha's son Xu also gathered followers to join Fu; Left Chancellor Rui considered sending troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Zha's son Xu also gathered followers to join Fu; Left Chancellor Rui considered sending troops against him.

sentences.zh: 王導曰：「今少發兵則不足以平寇，多發兵則根本空虛。

translations.literal: Wang Dao said: "If we send few troops they will not be enough to suppress the rebels; if we send many the foundation will be left empty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao said, "If we send few troops they will not be enough to suppress the rebels; if we send many our base will be left empty.

sentences.zh: 續族弟黃門侍郎莚，忠果有謀，請獨使莚往，足以誅續。」

translations.literal: Xu's clansman, Palace Attendant Zhou Yan, is loyal, resolute, and resourceful; I ask that Yan alone be sent—he will be enough to execute Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Xu's clansman, Palace Attendant Zhou Yan, is loyal, resolute, and resourceful. Send Yan alone—he will be enough to kill Xu."

sentences.zh: 睿從之。

translations.literal: Rui agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Rui agreed.

sentences.zh: 莚晝夜兼行，至郡，將入，遇續於門，謂續曰：「當與君共詣孔府君，有所論。」

translations.literal: Yan traveled day and night, reached the commandery, and was about to enter when he met Xu at the gate and said to Xu: "I should go with you to Lord Kong the Administrator—there is something to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: Yan traveled day and night, reached the commandery, and was about to enter when he met Xu at the gate and said, "Come with me to Administrator Kong—there is something to discuss."

sentences.zh: 續不肯入，莚牽逼與俱。

translations.literal: Xu would not enter; Yan pulled and forced him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Xu would not enter; Yan pulled and forced him to go along.

sentences.zh: 坐定，莚謂孔侃曰：「府君何以置賊在坐？」

translations.literal: When they were seated, Yan said to Kong Kan: "My lord, why do you seat a rebel here?"
translations.idiomatic: When they were seated, Yan said to Kong Kan, "My lord, why do you seat a rebel here?"

sentences.zh: 續衣中常置刀，即操刀逼莚，莚叱郡傳教吳曾格殺之。

translations.literal: Xu always kept a knife in his clothes; he immediately drew it and pressed on Yan; Yan shouted for the commandery instructor Wu Zeng to strike and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu always kept a knife in his clothes; he immediately drew it and pressed on Yan. Yan shouted for the commandery instructor Wu Zeng to strike and kill him.

sentences.zh: 莚因欲誅勰，札不聽，委罪於從兄邵而誅之。

translations.literal: Yan then wished to execute Xie; Zha would not permit it and shifted blame to his cousin Shao, who was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then wished to execute Xie; Zha would not permit it and shifted blame to his cousin Shao, who was executed.

sentences.zh: 莚不歸家省母，遂長驅而去，母狼狽追之。

translations.literal: Yan did not return home to visit his mother but drove straight on; his mother pursued him in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Yan did not return home to visit his mother but drove straight on; his mother pursued him in disarray.

sentences.zh: 睿以札為吳興太守，莚為太子右衛率。

translations.literal: Rui made Zha Governor of Wu Xing and Yan Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Rui made Zha Governor of Wu Xing and Yan Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 以周氏吳之豪望，故不窮治，撫勰如舊。

translations.literal: Because the Zhou clan was a great power in Wu, he did not pursue the matter to the end but treated Xie as before.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Zhou clan was a great power in Wu, he did not pursue the matter to the end but treated Xie as before.

sentences.zh: 詔平東將軍宋哲屯華陰。

translations.literal: An edict ordered General Who Pacifies the East Song Zhe to encamp at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered General Who Pacifies the East Song Zhe to encamp at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 成主雄立後任氏。

translations.literal: Cheng ruler Xiong established Lady Ren as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng ruler Li Xiong established Lady Ren as empress.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子，以琅邪王睿為丞相、大都督、督中外諸軍事，南陽王保為相國，荀組為太尉、領豫州牧，劉琨為司空、都督並、冀、幽三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingzi, Prince of Langye Rui was made Chancellor, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs at home and abroad; Prince of Nanyang Bao was made Chancellor of State; Xun Zu was made Grand Minister of Works and concurrently Governor of Yuzhou; Liu Kun was made Minister of Works and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Bing, Ji, and You.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingzi, Prince of Langye Rui was made Chancellor, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs at home and abroad; Prince of Nanyang Bao Chancellor of State; Xun Zu Grand Minister of Works and concurrently Governor of Yuzhou; and Liu Kun Minister of Works and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Bing, Ji, and You.

sentences.zh: 琨辭司空不受。

translations.literal: Kun declined the post of Minister of Works and did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Kun declined Minister of Works and did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 南陽王模之敗也，都尉陳安往歸世子保於秦州，保命安將千餘人討叛羌，寵待甚厚。

translations.literal: When Prince of Nanyang Mo was defeated, Commandant Chen An went to join the heir Bao in Qinzhou; Bao ordered An to lead more than a thousand men to suppress rebellious Qiang and treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Nanyang Mo was defeated, Commandant Chen An went to join the heir Bao in Qinzhou. Bao ordered An to lead more than a thousand men to suppress rebellious Qiang and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 保將張春疾之，譖安，雲有異志，請除之，保不許；

translations.literal: Bao's general Zhang Chun envied him, slandered An, saying he had ulterior designs, and asked that he be removed; Bao did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Bao's general Zhang Chun envied him, slandered An as having ulterior designs, and asked that he be removed; Bao refused;

sentences.zh: 春輒伏刺客以刺安。

translations.literal: Chun then secretly set assassins to stab An.
translations.idiomatic: Chun then secretly set assassins to stab An.

sentences.zh: 安被創，馳還隴城，遣使詣保，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: An was wounded, galloped back to Longcheng, and sent envoys to Bao with tribute unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: An was wounded, galloped back to Longcheng, and continued sending envoys and tribute to Bao.

sentences.zh: 詔進拓跋猗盧爵為代王，置官屬，食代、常山二郡。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Tuoba Yilu to Prince of Dai, established his staff, and granted him the revenues of Dai and Changshan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict advanced Tuoba Yilu to Prince of Dai, established his staff, and granted him the revenues of Dai and Changshan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 猗盧請并州從事雁門莫含於劉琨，琨遣之。

translations.literal: Yilu requested Bingzhou Registrar Mo Han of Yanmen from Liu Kun, and Kun sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu requested Bingzhou Registrar Mo Han of Yanmen from Liu Kun, and Kun sent him.

sentences.zh: 含不欲行，琨曰：「以并州單弱，吾之不材，而能自存於胡、羯之間者，代王之力也。

translations.literal: Han did not wish to go; Kun said: "Bingzhou is isolated and weak; that I, unworthy as I am, can survive among the Hu and Jie is due to the Prince of Dai's power.
translations.idiomatic: Han did not wish to go. Kun said, "Bingzhou is isolated and weak; that I, unworthy as I am, can survive among the Hu and Jie is due to the Prince of Dai's power.

sentences.zh: 吾傾身竭貲，以長子為質而奉之者，庶幾為朝廷雪大恥也。

translations.literal: I have poured out my person and wealth and offered my eldest son as hostage to serve him, hoping thereby to wash away the great shame of the court.
translations.idiomatic: I have poured out my person and wealth and offered my eldest son as hostage to serve him, hoping thereby to wash away the great shame of the court.

sentences.zh: 卿欲為忠臣，奈何惜共事之小誠，而忘徇國之大節乎？

translations.literal: You wish to be a loyal minister—how can you cherish a small private loyalty in serving together and forget the great duty of serving the state?
translations.idiomatic: You wish to be a loyal minister—how can you cherish small private loyalty and forget the great duty of serving the state?

sentences.zh: 往事大王，為之腹心，乃一州之所賴也。」

translations.literal: Go serve the prince as his trusted confidant—you will be what the whole province relies upon."
translations.idiomatic: Go serve the prince as his trusted confidant—you will be what the whole province relies upon."

sentences.zh: 含遂行。

translations.literal: Han then went.
translations.idiomatic: Han then went.

sentences.zh: 猗盧甚重之，常與參大計。

translations.literal: Yilu valued him highly and often consulted him on major plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu valued him highly and often consulted him on major plans.

sentences.zh: 猗盧用法嚴，國人犯法者，或舉部就誅，老幼相攜而行，人問：「何之？」

translations.literal: Yilu applied the law strictly; when people of the state violated the law, sometimes whole clans went to execution, old and young leading one another along. Someone asked: "Where are you going?"
translations.idiomatic: Yilu applied the law strictly; when people violated the law, sometimes whole clans went to execution, old and young leading one another along. Someone asked, "Where are you going?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「往就死。」

translations.literal: They said: "To go and die."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "To go and die."

sentences.zh: 無一人敢逃匿者。

translations.literal: Not one dared flee or hide.
translations.idiomatic: Not one dared flee or hide.

sentences.zh: 王敦遣陶侃、甘卓等討杜弢，前後數十戰，弢將士多死，乃請降於丞相睿，睿不許。

translations.literal: Wang Dun sent Tao Kan, Gan Zhuo, and others to attack Du Tao; after dozens of battles in which many of Tao's officers and soldiers died, he asked to surrender to Chancellor Rui, but Rui did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun sent Tao Kan, Gan Zhuo, and others to attack Du Tao. After dozens of battles in which many of Tao's officers and soldiers died, he asked to surrender to Chancellor Rui, but Rui refused.

sentences.zh: 弢遺南平太守應詹書，自陳昔與詹「共討樂鄉，本同休戚。

translations.literal: Tao sent a letter to Nanping Governor Ying Zhan, stating that formerly with Zhan "we campaigned together at Le Township and shared the same weal and woe.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sent a letter to Nanping Governor Ying Zhan, stating that formerly with Zhan "we campaigned together at Le Township and shared the same weal and woe.

sentences.zh: 後在湘中，懼死求生，遂相結聚。

translations.literal: Later in Xiang province, fearing death and seeking life, they then banded together.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in Xiang province, fearing death and desperate to live, they banded together.

sentences.zh: 倘以舊交之情，為明枉直，使得輸誠盟府，廁列義徒，或北清中原，或西取李雄，以贖前愆，雖死之日，猶生之年也！」

translations.literal: If by the bond of old friendship you would clarify right and wrong, enable me to offer my loyalty to the alliance government, be numbered among the righteous followers, whether to clear the Central Plains in the north or seize Li Xiong in the west, to atone for past faults—even on the day I die, it would be as if I lived!"
translations.idiomatic: If out of our old friendship you would set right what was wrong, let me pledge loyalty to the alliance government and stand among its righteous servants—whether by clearing the Central Plains in the north or taking Li Xiong in the west, to redeem my past crimes. Though I die, it would be as though I still lived!"

sentences.zh: 詹為啟呈其書，且言「弢，益州秀才，素有清望，為鄉人所逼。

translations.literal: Zhan forwarded and presented the letter, also saying "Tao, a licentiate of Yizhou, has long enjoyed a clean reputation and was forced by his countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan forwarded the letter and added, "Tao, a licentiate of Yizhou, has long enjoyed a fine reputation and was driven to this by his countrymen.

sentences.zh: 今悔惡歸善，宜命使扶納，以息江、湘之民！」

translations.literal: Now regretting evil and returning to goodness, you should send envoys to support and accept him, to pacify the people of the Jiang and Xiang regions!"
translations.idiomatic: He now repents and turns to virtue. You should send envoys to receive and support him and give peace to the people of the Jiang and Xiang!"

sentences.zh: 睿乃使前南海太守王運受弢降，赦其反逆之罪，以弢為巴東監軍。

translations.literal: Rui then sent former Nanhai Governor Wang Yun to accept Tao's surrender, pardoned his crime of rebellion, and made Tao Supervisor of the Army of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Rui then sent former Nanhai Governor Wang Yun to accept Tao's surrender, pardoned his rebellion, and appointed him Supervisor of the Army of Badong.

sentences.zh: 弢既受命，諸將猶攻之不已。

translations.literal: Once Tao had accepted the appointment, the generals still pressed the attack without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tao had accepted the appointment, the generals kept attacking without letup.

sentences.zh: 弢不勝憤怒，遂殺運復反，遣其將杜弘、張彥殺臨川內史謝擒，遂陷豫章。

translations.literal: Tao, unable to contain his rage, killed Yun and rebelled again, sent his generals Du Hong and Zhang Yan to kill Linchuan Administrator Xie Qin, and then captured Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, unable to contain his fury, killed Yun and rebelled again. He sent his generals Du Hong and Zhang Yan to kill Linchuan Administrator Xie Qin and then took Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 三月，周訪擊彥，斬之，弘奔臨賀。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhou Fang attacked Yan, beheaded him; Hong fled to Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhou Fang attacked Zhang Yan, beheaded him, and Du Hong fled to Linhe.

sentences.zh: 漢大赦，改元建元。

translations.literal: Han proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 雨血於漢東宮延明殿，太弟乂惡之，以問太傅崔瑋、太保許遐。

translations.literal: Blood rained in the Eastern Palace's Yanming Hall in Han; the Grand Younger Brother Yi took it as an ill omen and questioned Grand Tutor Cui Wei and Grand Protector Xu Xia about it.
translations.idiomatic: Blood rained in Han's Eastern Palace at Yanming Hall. Grand Younger Brother Liu Yi took it as an ill omen and asked Grand Tutor Cui Wei and Grand Protector Xu Xia what it meant.

sentences.zh: 瑋、遐說乂曰：「主上往日以殿下為太弟者，欲以安眾心耳；

translations.literal: Wei and Xia advised Yi, saying: "The sovereign formerly made Your Highness Grand Younger Brother in order to calm the hearts of the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Xia urged Yi, saying, "The sovereign made Your Highness Grand Younger Brother in the first place only to calm the people's hearts;

sentences.zh: 其志在晉王久矣，王公已下莫不希旨附之。

translations.literal: his intent has long been with the Prince of Jin; from the kings down, none fail to read his wishes and attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: his heart has long been set on the Prince of Jin. From the kings downward, all have read his wishes and rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 今復以晉王為相國，羽儀威重，逾於東宮，萬機之事，無不由之，諸王皆置營兵以為羽翼，事勢已去；

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Jin has again been made Chancellor; his ceremonial guard and majesty exceed those of the Eastern Palace; affairs of state all pass through him; all the princes have stationed camp troops as wings for him—the situation is already lost;
translations.idiomatic: Now the Prince of Jin has been made Chancellor again. His retinue and authority surpass the Eastern Palace's; every affair of state passes through him; every prince keeps camp troops as his wings. The tide has already turned against you;

sentences.zh: 殿下非徒不得立也，朝夕且有不測之危，不如早為之計。

translations.literal: Your Highness will not merely fail to succeed to the throne; morning and evening you will face unpredictable peril—it would be better to act early.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness will not merely fail to inherit the throne—you will soon face unpredictable danger morning and night. Better to act while there is still time.

sentences.zh: 今四衛精兵不減五千，相國輕佻，正煩一刺客耳。

translations.literal: Now the four guards' crack troops number no fewer than five thousand; the Chancellor is frivolous and reckless—one assassin is all that is needed.
translations.idiomatic: The four guards still have no fewer than five thousand elite troops. The Chancellor is frivolous and reckless—a single assassin would suffice.

sentences.zh: 大將軍無日不出，其營可襲而取；

translations.literal: The Grand General goes out every day without fail; his camp can be taken by surprise;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General goes out every day without fail. His camp can be seized in a surprise attack;

sentences.zh: 餘王並幼，固易奪也。

translations.literal: the remaining princes are all young and would naturally be easy to seize from.
translations.idiomatic: the other princes are all young and would be easy to overpower.

sentences.zh: 苟殿下有意，二萬精兵指顧可得，鼓行入雲龍門，宿衛之士，孰不倒戈以迎殿下者！

translations.literal: If Your Highness has the will, twenty thousand crack troops can be had at a gesture; marching with drums beating through the Cloud Dragon Gate, which of the palace guards would not cast aside their weapons to welcome Your Highness!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness is willing, twenty thousand elite troops can be raised at a word. March with drums through the Cloud Dragon Gate—what palace guard would not drop his weapon to welcome you!

sentences.zh: 大司馬不慮其為異也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal would not worry that this was treason."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal would never suspect treason."

sentences.zh: 乂弗從。

translations.literal: Yi did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 東宮舍人荀裕告瑋、遐勸乂謀反，漢主聰收瑋、遐於詔獄，假以他事殺之。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace Attendant Xun Yu reported that Wei and Xia had urged Yi to rebel; Han ruler Cong seized Wei and Xia in the imperial prison and killed them on false charges.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace Attendant Xun Yu reported that Wei and Xia had urged Yi to rebel. Han ruler Liu Cong seized them in the imperial prison and killed them on trumped-up charges.

sentences.zh: 使冠威將軍卜抽將兵監守東宮，禁乂不聽朝會。

translations.literal: He sent General of the Crown Prince's Military Might Bu Chou with troops to guard and supervise the Eastern Palace, forbidding Yi to attend court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General of the Crown Prince's Military Might Bu Chou with troops to guard the Eastern Palace and barred Yi from attending court.

sentences.zh: 乂憂懼不知所為，上表乞為庶人，並除諸子之封，褒美晉王，請以為嗣；

translations.literal: Yi, anxious and afraid and at a loss what to do, submitted a memorial asking to be made a commoner, also requesting removal of his sons' enfeoffments, praised the Prince of Jin, and asked that he be made heir;
translations.idiomatic: Yi, fearful and at a loss, submitted a memorial asking to be reduced to commoner status, to have his sons' enfeoffments revoked, and praising the Prince of Jin, asked that he be made heir;

sentences.zh: 抽抑而弗通。

translations.literal: Chou suppressed it and did not pass it through.
translations.idiomatic: Chou suppressed the memorial and would not forward it.

sentences.zh: 漢青州刺史曹嶷盡得齊、魯間郡縣，自鎮臨菑，有眾十餘萬，臨河置戍。

translations.literal: Han's Inspector of Qingzhou Cao Yi fully held the commanderies and counties between Qi and Lu, established himself at Linzi, had a force of more than a hundred thousand, and set garrisons along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Inspector of Qingzhou Cao Yi held all the commanderies and counties between Qi and Lu, made Linzi his base, mustered more than a hundred thousand men, and posted garrisons along the river.

sentences.zh: 石勒表稱：「嶷有專據東方之志，請討之。」

translations.literal: Shi Le submitted a memorial saying: "Yi harbors an intent to hold the east by force; I request permission to attack him."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le submitted a memorial: "Cao Yi intends to hold the east on his own authority. I ask leave to attack him."

sentences.zh: 漢主聰恐勒滅嶷，不可複製，弗許。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong feared that if Le destroyed Yi, he could not be brought under control again, and did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong feared that if Shi Le destroyed Cao Yi, he could never be controlled again, and refused.

sentences.zh: 聰納中護軍靳准二女月光、月華，立月光為上皇后，劉貴妃為左皇后，月華為右皇后。

translations.literal: Cong took the two daughters of Central Guard General Jin Zhun, Yueguang and Yuehua, as consorts; he made Yueguang Senior Empress, Consort Liu Left Empress, and Yuehua Right Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong took the two daughters of Central Guard General Jin Zhun, Yueguang and Yuehua, as consorts. He made Yueguang Senior Empress, Consort Liu Left Empress, and Yuehua Right Empress.

sentences.zh: 左司隸陳元達極諫，以為：「並立三後，非禮也。」

translations.literal: Left Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Yuanda remonstrated strenuously, stating: "Establishing three empresses simultaneously is against ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Left Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Yuanda remonstrated forcefully, saying, "To establish three empresses at once is against ritual."

sentences.zh: 聰不悅，以元達為右光祿大夫，外示優崇，實奪其權。

translations.literal: Cong was displeased; he made Yuanda Grandee of Splendid Happiness on the Right—in outward show an honor, but in fact stripping him of power.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong was displeased. He made Yuanda Grandee of Splendid Happiness on the Right—an outward honor that in fact stripped him of power.

sentences.zh: 於是太尉范隆等皆請以位讓元達，聰乃復以元達為御史大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Commandant Fan Long and others all asked to yield their posts to Yuanda; Cong then restored Yuanda as Censor-in-Chief with the equal glory of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Grand Commandant Fan Long and others all offered to yield their posts to Yuanda. Liu Cong then restored Yuanda as Censor-in-Chief with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 月光有穢行，元達奏之，聰不得已廢之，月光慚恚自殺，聰恨元達。

translations.literal: Yueguang had licentious conduct; Yuanda memorialized it; Cong had no choice but to depose her; Yueguang, ashamed and enraged, killed herself; Cong resented Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang had disgraceful conduct. Yuanda reported it, and Liu Cong had no choice but to depose her. Yueguang, shamed and enraged, killed herself, and Liu Cong came to hate Yuanda.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 六月，盜發漢霸、杜二陵及薄太后陵，得金帛甚多，朝廷以用度不足，詔收其餘以實內府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, robbers opened the Han tombs at Ba and Du Mausoleums and Empress Dowager Bo's tomb, obtaining much gold and silk; the court, finding expenditures insufficient, ordered the remainder collected to fill the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, tomb robbers broke into the Han tombs at Ba and Du and Empress Dowager Bo's tomb and took much gold and silk. Because state expenses were insufficient, the court ordered what remained collected for the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi, general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 漢大司馬曜攻上黨，八月，癸亥，敗劉琨之眾於襄垣。

translations.literal: Han Grand Marshal Yao attacked Shangdang; in the eighth month, on guihai, he defeated Liu Kun's forces at Xiangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Grand Marshal Liu Yao attacked Shangdang. In the eighth month, on guihai, he defeated Liu Kun's army at Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 曜欲進攻陽曲，漢主聰遣使謂之曰：「長安未平，宜以為先。」

translations.literal: Yao wished to advance and attack Yangqu; Han ruler Cong sent a messenger telling him: "Chang'an is not yet pacified—that should come first."
translations.idiomatic: Yao wished to press on and attack Yangqu. Han ruler Liu Cong sent a messenger telling him, "Chang'an is not yet pacified. That must come first."

sentences.zh: 曜乃還屯蒲板。

translations.literal: Yao then returned and encamped at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Yao then withdrew and encamped at Puban.

sentences.zh: 陶侃與杜弢相攻，弢使王貢出挑戰，侃遙謂之曰：「杜弢為益州小吏，盜用庫錢，父死不奔喪。

translations.literal: Tao Kan and Du Tao fought each other; Tao sent Wang Gong out to challenge; Kan called to him from afar: "Du Tao was a petty clerk in Yizhou who embezzled treasury funds and did not rush home when his father died.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan and Du Tao fought each other. Tao sent Wang Gong out to challenge. Kan called to him from afar, "Du Tao was a petty clerk in Yizhou who stole from the treasury and did not go home when his father died.

sentences.zh: 卿本佳人，何為隨之！

translations.literal: You are a fine man by nature—why follow him!
translations.idiomatic: You are a good man by nature—why follow him!

sentences.zh: 天下寧有白頭賊邪？」

translations.literal: Can there be bandits with white hair in the world?"
translations.idiomatic: Surely there are no bandits with white hair in this world?"

sentences.zh: 貢初橫腳馬上，聞侃言，斂容下腳。

translations.literal: Gong had at first sat astride with legs crossed on his horse; hearing Kan's words, he composed himself and brought his leg down.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had been sitting cross-legged on his horse. Hearing Kan's words, he straightened up and lowered his leg.

sentences.zh: 侃知可動，復遣使諭之，截發為信，貢遂降於侃。

translations.literal: Kan knew he could be moved; he again sent envoys to persuade him, cutting off his hair as pledge; Gong then surrendered to Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Kan saw that he could be swayed and sent envoys again to persuade him, cutting off his own hair as pledge. Gong then surrendered to Kan.

sentences.zh: 弢眾潰，遁走，道死。

translations.literal: Tao's forces collapsed; he fled and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao's army collapsed. He fled and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 侃與南平太守應詹進克長沙，湘州悉平。

translations.literal: Kan and Nanping Governor Ying Zhan advanced and captured Changsha; Xiang province was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Kan and Nanping Governor Ying Zhan advanced and took Changsha. All of Xiang province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 丞相睿承製赦其所部，進王敦鎮東大將軍，加都督江、揚、荊、湘、交、廣六州諸軍事、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Chancellor Rui, acting on the decree, pardoned those under his jurisdiction; Wang Dun was promoted to Great General Who Pacifies the East, with added authority as commander-in-chief of all military affairs in the six provinces of Jiang, Yang, Jing, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang, and Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Rui, acting on imperial authority, pardoned those under his command and promoted Wang Dun to Great General Who Pacifies the East, with added authority as commander-in-chief of military affairs in Jiang, Yang, Jing, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang and as Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敦始自選置刺史以下，浸益驕橫。

translations.literal: Dun began selecting and appointing governors and officials below that rank himself, and grew increasingly arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Dun began appointing governors and lower officials on his own authority and grew ever more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 初，王如之降也，敦從弟稜愛如驍勇，請敦配己麾下。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Ru surrendered, Dun's cousin Ling admired Ru's fierce valor and asked Dun to assign him to his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Ru surrendered, Dun's cousin Ling admired Ru's fierce courage and asked Dun to place him under his own command.

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「此輩險悍難畜，汝性狷急，不能容養，更成禍端。」

translations.literal: Dun said: "These men are treacherous and fierce, hard to keep; your nature is impetuous and narrow—you cannot tolerate and nurture them; it will only become a source of calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, "Those men are treacherous and fierce and hard to control. Your nature is impetuous and narrow—you cannot keep them in hand. It will only breed disaster."

sentences.zh: 稜固請，乃與之。

translations.literal: Ling pressed his request firmly, and Dun gave Ru to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ling pressed his request, and Dun gave Ru to him.

sentences.zh: 稜置左右，甚加寵遇。

translations.literal: Ling placed Ru at his side and favored him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Ling kept Ru at his side and favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 如數與敦諸將角射爭鬥，稜杖之，如深以為恥。

translations.literal: Ru repeatedly competed in archery and brawled with Dun's generals; Ling beat him with a staff; Ru deeply took it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ru repeatedly competed in archery and quarreled with Dun's generals. Ling beat him with a staff, and Ru took it as a deep humiliation.

sentences.zh: 及敦潛畜異志，稜每諫之。

translations.literal: When Dun secretly harbored rebellious intent, Ling admonished him each time.
