translations.idiomatic: When Dun secretly nursed rebellious ambitions, Ling admonished him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 敦怒其異己，密使人激如令殺稜。

translations.literal: Dun, angered that Ling opposed him, secretly sent someone to incite Ru to kill Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, angered that Ling opposed him, secretly sent someone to goad Ru into killing Ling.

sentences.zh: 如因閒宴，請劍舞為歡，稜許之。

translations.literal: Ru took advantage of a casual banquet to request a sword dance for amusement; Ling agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At a casual banquet Ru asked to perform a sword dance for amusement, and Ling agreed.

sentences.zh: 如舞劍漸前，稜惡而呵之，如直前殺稜。

translations.literal: As Ru danced with his sword he gradually advanced; Ling, displeased, shouted at him; Ru thrust forward and killed Ling.
translations.idiomatic: As Ru danced he edged forward with his sword. Ling, displeased, shouted at him. Ru lunged forward and killed him.

sentences.zh: 敦聞之，陽驚，亦捕如誅之。

translations.literal: When Dun heard of it, he feigned shock and also captured and executed Ru.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun heard of it, he feigned shock and had Ru captured and executed as well.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷聞張光死，以侍中第五猗為安南將軍，監荊、梁、益、寧四州諸軍事、荊州刺史，自武關出。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court heard that Zhang Guang had died, it made Palace Attendant Di Yi General Who Pacifies the South, with authority over all military affairs in the four provinces of Jing, Liang, Yi, and Ning and Governor of Jingzhou, to set out from Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the court learned that Zhang Guang had died, it appointed Palace Attendant Di Yi General Who Pacifies the South, with authority over military affairs in Jing, Liang, Yi, and Ning and as Governor of Jingzhou, to march out from Wuguan.

sentences.zh: 杜曾迎猗於襄陽，為兄子娶猗女，遂聚兵萬人，與猗分據漢、沔。

translations.literal: Du Zeng received Yi at Xiangyang, had his nephew marry Yi's daughter, then gathered ten thousand troops and with Yi divided control of the Han and Mian regions.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng received Di Yi at Xiangyang, had his nephew marry Yi's daughter, gathered ten thousand troops, and with Yi divided control of the Han and Mian.

sentences.zh: 陶侃既破杜弢，乘勝進擊曾，有輕曾之志。

translations.literal: After Tao Kan had defeated Du Tao, he pressed his victory to attack Zeng, holding Zeng in slight regard.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Kan had defeated Du Tao, he pressed his victory against Du Zeng and held him in slight regard.

sentences.zh: 司馬魯恬諫曰：「凡戰，當先料其將。

translations.literal: Army Aide Lu Tian remonstrated: "In every battle, one should first assess the enemy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Army Aide Lu Tian remonstrated, "In every battle one must first judge the enemy commander.

sentences.zh: 今使君諸將，無及曾者，未易可逼也。」

translations.literal: Now none of the lord's generals match Zeng; he cannot easily be pressed."
translations.idiomatic: None of your generals today equals Du Zeng. He cannot easily be forced."

sentences.zh: 侃不從，進圍曾於石城。

translations.literal: Kan did not accept and advanced to besiege Zeng at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kan would not listen and advanced to besiege Zeng at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 曾軍多騎兵，密開門突侃陳，出其後，反擊之，侃兵死者數百人。

translations.literal: Zeng's army had many cavalry; he secretly opened the gate and burst into Kan's formation, came out behind him, and counterattacked; several hundred of Kan's soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng's army had many cavalry. He secretly opened the gate, burst into Kan's lines, got behind him, and counterattacked. Several hundred of Kan's men were killed.

sentences.zh: 曾將趨順陽，下馬拜侃，告辭而去。

translations.literal: Zeng was about to head for Shunyang; he dismounted, bowed to Kan, took his leave, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng was about to march for Shunyang. He dismounted, bowed to Kan, took his leave, and went.

sentences.zh: 時荀崧都督荊州江北諸軍事，屯宛，曾引兵圍之。

translations.literal: At the time Xun Song was commander-in-chief of all military affairs north of the Yangzi in Jingzhou, encamped at Wan; Zeng led troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xun Song commanded military affairs north of the Yangzi in Jingzhou and was encamped at Wan. Du Zeng led troops to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 崧兵少食盡，欲求救於故吏襄城太守石覽。

translations.literal: Song's troops were few and food was exhausted; he wished to seek rescue from his former subordinate Xiangcheng Governor Shi Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Song's troops were few and provisions were exhausted. He wanted to seek help from his former subordinate Xiangcheng Governor Shi Lan.

sentences.zh: 崧小女灌，年十三，帥勇士數十人，逾城突圍夜出，且戰且前，遂達覽所；

translations.literal: Song's young daughter Guan, age thirteen, led several dozen brave men, crossed the wall and broke out by night, fighting as she advanced, and reached Lan's position;
translations.idiomatic: Song's young daughter Guan, thirteen years old, led several dozen brave men over the wall in a night breakout, fighting as she went, and reached Lan;

sentences.zh: 又為崧書，求救於南中郎將周訪。

translations.literal: she also wrote a letter for Song seeking rescue from Colonel-in-Chief of the South Zhou Fang.
translations.idiomatic: she also wrote a letter for Song asking Zhou Fang, Colonel-in-Chief of the South, for help.

sentences.zh: 訪遣子扶帥兵三千，與覽共救崧，曾乃遁去。

translations.literal: Fang sent his son Fu leading three thousand troops; together with Lan they rescued Song, and Zeng then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sent his son Fu with three thousand troops. Together with Lan they relieved Song, and Du Zeng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 曾復致箋於崧，求討丹水賊以自效，崧許之。

translations.literal: Zeng again sent a letter to Song asking to campaign against the bandits of Danshui to prove his loyalty; Song agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng again wrote to Song offering to attack the bandits of Danshui to prove his loyalty, and Song agreed.

sentences.zh: 陶侃遺崧書曰：「杜曾凶狡，所謂『鴟梟食母之物』。

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent Song a letter saying: "Du Zeng is vicious and cunning—the so-called 'owl that devours its mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan wrote to Song, "Du Zeng is vicious and cunning—what people call 'the owl that eats its own mother.'

sentences.zh: 此人不死，州土未寧，足下當識吾言！」

translations.literal: While this man lives, the province will not be at peace—you must heed my words!"
translations.idiomatic: While this man lives, the province will never know peace. You must heed my words!"

sentences.zh: 崧以宛中兵少，藉曾為外援，不從。

translations.literal: Song, with few troops at Wan and relying on Zeng as external support, did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Song, with few troops at Wan and relying on Zeng as outside support, would not listen.

sentences.zh: 曾復帥流亡二千餘人圍襄陽，數日，不克而還。

translations.literal: Zeng again led more than two thousand displaced followers to besiege Xiangyang; after several days, failing to take it, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng again led more than two thousand displaced followers to besiege Xiangyang. After several days he failed to take it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王敦嬖人吳興錢鳳，疾陶侃之功，屢毀之。

translations.literal: Wang Dun's favorite Wu Xing Qian Feng, jealous of Tao Kan's achievements, repeatedly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's favorite Qian Feng of Wu Xing, jealous of Tao Kan's achievements, repeatedly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 侃將還江陵，欲詣敦自陳。

translations.literal: Kan was about to return to Jiangling and wished to visit Dun to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: As Kan was about to return to Jiangling, he wanted to visit Dun and explain himself.

sentences.zh: 朱伺及安定皇甫方回諫曰：「公入必不出。」

translations.literal: Zhu Si and Huangfu Fanghui of Anding remonstrated: "If you enter, you will surely not come out."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si and Huangfu Fanghui of Anding remonstrated, "If you go in, you will surely not come out."

sentences.zh: 侃不從。

translations.literal: Kan did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Kan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既至，敦留侃不遣，左轉廣州刺史，以其從弟丞相軍咨祭酒廙為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Dun detained Kan and would not release him; he transferred Kan to the left as Governor of Guangzhou and made his cousin, Chancellor's Army Consultation and Sacrificial Officer Mei, Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, Dun detained him and would not let him go. He transferred Kan to Governor of Guangzhou and made his cousin Mei, the Chancellor's Army Consultation and Sacrificial Officer, Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 荊州將吏鄭攀、馬俊等詣敦，上書留侃，敦怒，不許。

translations.literal: Jingzhou officers and officials Zheng Pan, Ma Jun, and others went to Dun and submitted a petition asking that Kan be kept; Dun was angry and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou officers and officials Zheng Pan, Ma Jun, and others went to Dun and petitioned to keep Kan. Dun was angry and refused.

sentences.zh: 攀等以侃始滅大賊，而更被黜，眾情憤惋；

translations.literal: Pan and the others, because Kan had just destroyed a great rebel only to be dismissed again, roused public indignation and resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Pan and the others, because Kan had just destroyed a great rebel only to be dismissed again, stirred public anger;

sentences.zh: 又以廙忌戾難事，遂帥其徒三千人屯溳口，西迎杜曾。

translations.literal: and because Mei was harsh, spiteful, and hard to serve, they then led their three thousand followers to encamp at Yun Kou and went west to welcome Du Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: and because Mei was harsh and difficult to serve, they led three thousand men to encamp at Yun Kou and went west to welcome Du Zeng.

sentences.zh: 溳為攀等所襲，奔於江安。

translations.literal: Mei was attacked by Pan and the others and fled to Jiang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mei was attacked by Pan and the others and fled to Jiang'an.

sentences.zh: 杜曾與攀等北迎第五猗以拒廙。

translations.literal: Du Zeng with Pan and the others went north to welcome Di Yi to resist Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng and Pan and the others went north to welcome Di Yi and resist Mei.

sentences.zh: 廙督諸軍討曾，復為曾所敗。

translations.literal: Mei commanded the various armies to attack Zeng and was again defeated by Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Mei commanded the armies against Du Zeng and was defeated by him again.

sentences.zh: 敦意攀承侃風旨，被甲持矛將殺侃，出而復還者數四。

translations.literal: Dun thought Pan was acting on Kan's instructions; armored and holding a spear, he was about to kill Kan, going out and returning again four times.
translations.idiomatic: Dun thought Pan was acting on Kan's orders. Armored and spear in hand, he was about to kill Kan, going out and coming back four times without doing it.

sentences.zh: 侃正色曰：「使君雄斷，當裁天下，何此不決乎！」

translations.literal: Kan said gravely: "My lord, you are bold and decisive—you should judge the realm; why this indecision!"
translations.idiomatic: Kan said gravely, "My lord, you are bold and decisive enough to judge the realm. Why this hesitation!"

sentences.zh: 因起如廁。

translations.literal: He then rose and went to the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Then he rose and went to the privy.

sentences.zh: 咨議參軍梅陶、長史陳頒言於敦曰：「周訪與侃親姻，如左右手，安有斷人左手而右手不應者乎！」

translations.literal: Consultation Official Army Aide Mei Tao and Chief Clerk Chen Ban said to Dun: "Zhou Fang and Kan are related by marriage, like left hand and right hand—how can you cut off a man's left hand and expect the right not to respond!"
translations.idiomatic: Consultation Official Army Aide Mei Tao and Chief Clerk Chen Ban said to Dun, "Zhou Fang and Kan are related by marriage, like left hand and right hand. Cut off a man's left hand—will the right not strike back?"

sentences.zh: 敦意解，乃設盛饌以餞之，侃便夜發，敦引其子瞻為參軍。

translations.literal: Dun's anger eased; he then set out a lavish feast to send Kan off; Kan departed that very night; Dun took his son Zhan as Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's anger eased. He set out a lavish feast to send Kan off. Kan left that same night, and Dun took his son Zhan on as Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 初，交州刺史顧秘卒，州人以秘子壽領州事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiaozhou Inspector Gu Mi died; the people of the province had Mi's son Shou take charge of provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiaozhou Inspector Gu Mi died, and the people of the province had Mi's son Shou take charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 帳下督梁碩起兵攻壽，殺之，碩遂專制交州。

translations.literal: Camp Supervisor Liang Shuo raised troops to attack Shou, killed him, and Shuo then seized sole control of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Camp Supervisor Liang Shuo raised troops, attacked Shou, killed him, and then seized sole control of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 王機自以盜據廣州，恐王敦討之，更求交州。

translations.literal: Wang Ji, having seized Guangzhou by force, feared Wang Dun would attack him and asked instead for Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, having seized Guangzhou by force, feared Wang Dun would attack him and asked to be transferred to Jiaozhou instead.

sentences.zh: 會杜弘詣機降，敦欲因機以討碩。

translations.literal: When Du Hong came to Ji to surrender, Dun wished to use Ji to attack Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Hong came to Wang Ji to surrender, Dun wanted to use Ji to attack Liang Shuo.

sentences.zh: 乃以降杜弘為機功，轉交州刺史。

translations.literal: He then made the surrendered Du Hong Ji's aide and transferred Ji to Governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed the surrendered Du Hong as Ji's lieutenant and transferred Ji to Governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 機至鬱林，碩迎前刺史脩則子湛行州事以拒之。

translations.literal: Ji reached Yulin; Shuo welcomed former governor Xiu Ze's son Zhan to conduct provincial affairs to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji reached Yulin. Shuo installed former governor Xiu Ze's son Zhan to conduct provincial affairs and resist him.

sentences.zh: 機不得進，乃更與杜弘及廣州將溫邵、交州秀才劉沈謀復還據廣州。

translations.literal: Ji could not advance; he then again plotted with Du Hong and Guangzhou general Wen Shao and Jiaozhou licentiate Liu Shen to return and seize Guangzhou once more.
translations.idiomatic: Ji could not advance. He then plotted again with Du Hong, Guangzhou general Wen Shao, and Jiaozhou licentiate Liu Shen to return and seize Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 陶侃至始興，州人皆言宜觀察形勢，不可輕進。

translations.literal: Tao Kan reached Shixing; the people of the province all said he should observe the situation and not advance rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan reached Shixing, the people of the province all said he should watch the situation and not advance rashly.

sentences.zh: 侃不聽，直至廣州，諸郡縣皆已迎機矣。

translations.literal: Kan did not listen; he pressed straight on to Guangzhou—but all the commanderies and counties had already welcomed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Kan would not listen. He pressed straight on to Guangzhou—but every commandery and county had already welcomed Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 杜弘遣使偽降，侃知其謀，進擊弘，破之，遂執劉沈於小桂。

translations.literal: Du Hong sent envoys feigning surrender; Kan knew his plot, advanced to attack Hong, defeated him, and then captured Liu Shen at Xiaogui.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong sent envoys feigning surrender. Kan saw through the ruse, attacked Hong, defeated him, and captured Liu Shen at Xiaogui.

sentences.zh: 遣督護許高討王機，走之。

translations.literal: He sent Supervising Protector Xu Gao to attack Wang Ji and put him to flight.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Supervising Protector Xu Gao against Wang Ji and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 機病死於道，高掘其屍，斬之。

translations.literal: Ji died of illness on the road; Gao dug up his corpse and beheaded it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji died of illness on the road. Gao dug up his corpse and beheaded it.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆請乘勝擊溫邵，侃笑曰：「吾威名已著，何事遣兵！

translations.literal: The generals all asked to press the victory and attack Wen Shao; Kan laughed and said: "My renown is already established—why send troops!
translations.idiomatic: The generals all urged a follow-up strike against Wen Shao. Kan laughed and said, "My renown is already established—why send troops!

sentences.zh: 但一函紙自定耳。」

translations.literal: A single letter will settle it."
translations.idiomatic: A single letter will settle it."

sentences.zh: 乃下書諭之。

translations.literal: He then issued a letter instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued a letter of instruction.

sentences.zh: 邵懼而走，追獲於始興。

translations.literal: Shao fled in fear and was pursued and captured at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Shao fled in fear and was pursued and captured at Shixing.

sentences.zh: 杜弘詣王敦降，廣州遂平。

translations.literal: Du Hong went to Wang Dun to surrender, and Guangzhou was finally pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong went to Wang Dun to surrender, and Guangzhou was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 侃在廣州無事，輒朝運百甓於齋外，暮運於齋內。

translations.literal: While Kan had nothing to do in Guangzhou, each morning he would carry a hundred bricks outside his study and each evening carry them back inside.
translations.idiomatic: While Tao Kan had nothing to do in Guangzhou, each morning he carried a hundred bricks outside his study and each evening carried them back in.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，答曰：「吾方致力中原，過爾優逸，恐不堪事，故自勞耳。」

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, he answered: "I am about to devote myself to the Central Plains; if I grow too comfortable and idle, I fear I will not be able to bear hardship when it comes—so I wear myself out on purpose."
translations.idiomatic: When people asked why, he answered, "I am about to devote myself to the Central Plains. If I grow too comfortable and idle, I fear I will not be able to bear hardship when it comes—so I wear myself out on purpose."

sentences.zh: 王敦以杜弘為將，寵任之。

translations.literal: Wang Dun made Du Hong a general and favored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun made Du Hong a general and favored and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 九月，漢主聰使大鴻臚賜石勒弓矢，策命勒為陝東伯，得專征伐，拜刺史、將軍、守宰，封列候，歲盡集上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Han Sovereign Cong sent the Grand Master of Ceremonies to bestow bows and arrows on Shi Le, issued an investiture appointing Le Marquis of East Shan, with authority to campaign independently, to appoint governors, generals, prefects, and magistrates, to enfeoff ranked marquises—all to assemble at court yearly.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Han Sovereign Liu Cong sent the Grand Master of Ceremonies to bestow bows and arrows on Shi Le and issued an investiture appointing him Marquis of East Shan, with authority to campaign independently, appoint governors, generals, prefects, and magistrates, and enfeoff ranked marquises—all of whom were to assemble at court each year.

sentences.zh: 漢大司馬曜寇北地，詔以麴允為大都督、驃騎將軍以御之。

translations.literal: Han Grand Marshal Yao raided Beidi; an edict made Qu Yun Grand Commander and Flying Cavalry General to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Grand Marshal Liu Yao raided Beidi. An edict appointed Qu Yun Grand Commander and Flying Cavalry General to resist him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以索綝為尚書僕射、都督宮城諸軍事。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Suo Lin was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Commander of All Military Affairs of the Palace City.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Suo Lin was made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Commander of All Military Affairs of the Palace City.

sentences.zh: 曜進拔馮翊，太守梁肅奔萬年。

translations.literal: Yao advanced and took Fengyi; Administrator Liang Su fled to Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Yao advanced and took Fengyi. Administrator Liang Su fled to Wannian.

sentences.zh: 曜轉寇上郡，麴允去黃白城，軍於靈武，以兵弱，不敢進。

translations.literal: Yao turned to raid Shang Commandery; Qu Yun left Huangbai City and encamped at Lingwu, but dared not advance due to weak forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yao turned to raid Shang Commandery. Qu Yun left Huangbai City and encamped at Lingwu, but his forces were too weak to advance.

sentences.zh: 帝屢徵兵於丞相保，保左右皆曰：「蝮蛇螫手，壯士斷腕。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly summoned troops from Chancellor Bao; Bao's attendants all said: "When a viper bites the hand, a strong man cuts off his wrist.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly summoned troops from Chancellor Bao. Bao's attendants all said, "When a viper bites the hand, a strong man cuts off his wrist.

sentences.zh: 今胡寇方盛，且宜斷隴道以觀其變。」

translations.literal: Now the barbarian raiders are at their height—it is better to cut the Long Road and watch how things develop."
translations.idiomatic: Now the barbarian raiders are at their height. Better to cut the Long Road and watch how things develop."

sentences.zh: 從事中郎裴詵曰：「今蛇已螫頭，頭可斷乎！」

translations.literal: Consultation Official Pei Shen said: "Now the viper has bitten the head—can the head be cut off!"
translations.idiomatic: Consultation Official Pei Shen said, "Now the viper has bitten the head—can the head be cut off?"

sentences.zh: 保乃以鎮軍將軍胡崧行前鋒都督，須諸軍集乃發。

translations.literal: Bao then made Army Stabilizing General Hu Song advance Vanguard Commander, to move only after all armies had assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Bao then made Army Stabilizing General Hu Song advance Vanguard Commander, to move only after all armies had assembled.

sentences.zh: 麴允欲奉帝往就保，索綝曰：「保得天子，必逞其私志。」

translations.literal: Qu Yun wished to bring the Emperor to Bao; Suo Lin said: "If Bao gets the Son of Heaven, he will surely indulge his private ambitions."
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun wished to bring the Emperor to Bao. Suo Lin said, "If Bao gets the Son of Heaven, he will surely indulge his private ambitions."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: So they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So they stopped.

sentences.zh: 於是自長安以西，不復貢奉朝廷，百官饑乏，采穭以自存。

translations.literal: Thus from Chang'an westward, tribute to the court ceased; officials and officers went hungry and gathered wild grains to survive.
translations.idiomatic: From Chang'an westward, tribute to the court ceased. Officials and officers went hungry and gathered wild grains to survive.

sentences.zh: 涼州軍士張冰得璽，文曰「皇帝行璽」，獻於張實，僚屬皆賀。

translations.literal: A Liangzhou soldier Zhang Bing obtained a seal bearing the inscription "Emperor's Traveling Seal" and presented it to Zhang Shi; his subordinates all congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: A Liangzhou soldier named Zhang Bing obtained a seal inscribed "Emperor's Traveling Seal" and presented it to Zhang Shi. His subordinates all congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 實曰：「是非人臣所得留。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "This is not something a subject may keep."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "This is not something a subject may keep."

sentences.zh: 遣使歸於長安。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to return it to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to return it to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 孝愍皇帝下建興四年（

translations.literal: Fourth year of Jianxing under Emperor Xiaomin (
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year of Jianxing of Emperor Min (

sentences.zh: 丙子，公元三一六年）

translations.literal: Bingzi, CE 316)
translations.idiomatic: year Bingzi, AD 316)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，司徒梁芬議追尊吳王晏，右僕射索綝等引魏明帝詔以為不可；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Minister of Education Liang Fen proposed posthumously honoring Prince of Wu Yan; Vice Director Suo Lin and others cited an edict of Emperor Ming of Wei to argue it would not be permissible;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Minister of Education Liang Fen proposed posthumously honoring Prince of Wu Liu Yan. Vice Director Suo Lin and others cited an edict of Emperor Ming of Wei to argue it was impermissible;

sentences.zh: 乃贈太保，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: they then granted him posthumous title Grand Mentor and gave the posthumous name Xiao ("Filial").
translations.idiomatic: they then granted him the posthumous title Grand Mentor and the posthumous name Xiao ("Filial").

sentences.zh: 漢中常侍王沈、宣懷、中宮僕射郭猗等，皆寵幸用事。

translations.literal: Han Palace Attendants Wang Shen, Xuan Huai, Palace Steward of the Inner Palace Guo Yi, and others—all were favored and held power.
translations.idiomatic: Han Palace Attendants Wang Shen and Xuan Huai, Palace Steward of the Inner Palace Guo Yi, and others—all were favored intimates who held real power.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰游宴後宮，或三日不醒，或百日不出；

translations.literal: Han Sovereign Cong feasted and played in the inner palace, sometimes not sober for three days, sometimes not emerging for a hundred days;
translations.idiomatic: Han Sovereign Liu Cong feasted and played in the inner palace, sometimes drunk for three days straight, sometimes not emerging for a hundred days;

sentences.zh: 自去冬不視朝，政事一委相國粲，唯殺生、除拜乃使沈等入白之。

translations.literal: since last winter he had not held court; all affairs were entrusted to Chancellor Zan; only executions and appointments were reported to him through Shen and the others.
translations.idiomatic: since last winter he had not held court. All affairs were entrusted to Chancellor Liu Zan; only executions and appointments were reported to him through Shen and the others.

sentences.zh: 沈等多不白，而自以其私意決之，故勳舊或不敘，而奸佞小人有數日至二千石者。

translations.literal: Shen and the others often did not report these but decided according to their private wishes—so meritorious veterans went unrewarded while villainous petty men could reach the rank of two-thousand-bushel officials within days.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the others often did not report these matters but decided them by their own whim—so meritorious veterans went unrewarded while villainous petty men could reach two-thousand-bushel rank within days.

sentences.zh: 軍旅歲起，將士無錢帛之賞，而後宮之家，賜及僮僕，動至數千萬。

translations.literal: Campaigns were launched year after year, yet soldiers received no rewards in coin or silk—while consorts' families and even their servants received gifts often running to tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns were launched year after year, yet soldiers received no rewards in coin or silk—while consorts' families and even their servants received gifts running to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 沈等車服、第捨逾於諸王，子弟中表為守令者三十餘人，皆貪殘為民害。

translations.literal: Shen and the others' carriages, robes, and mansions surpassed those of the princes; more than thirty of their sons, nephews, and cousins-in-law served as prefects and magistrates—all greedy and cruel, a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the others' carriages, robes, and mansions surpassed those of the princes. More than thirty of their sons, nephews, and cousins-in-law served as prefects and magistrates—all greedy and cruel, a scourge to the people.

sentences.zh: 靳准闔宗諂事之。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun's entire clan flattered and served them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun's entire clan flattered and served them.

sentences.zh: 郭猗與准皆有怨於太弟乂，猗謂相國粲曰：「殿下光文帝之世孫，主上之嫡子，四海莫不屬心，奈何欲以天下與太弟乎！

translations.literal: Guo Yi and Zhun both bore grudges against Grand Younger Brother Yi; Yi said to Chancellor Zan: "Your Highness is a great-grandson of Emperor Guangwen and the sovereign's eldest son by the consort—in all the realm none fail to look to you. Why would you want to give the empire to the Grand Younger Brother!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi and Jin Zhun both bore grudges against Grand Younger Brother Liu Yi. Yi said to Chancellor Liu Zan, "Your Highness is a great-grandson of Emperor Guangwen and the sovereign's eldest son by the consort—in all the realm none fail to look to you. Why would you want to give the empire to the Grand Younger Brother?

sentences.zh: 且臣聞太弟與大將軍謀因三月上巳大宴作亂，事成，許以主上為太上皇，大將軍為皇太子，又許衛軍為大單于。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear the Grand Younger Brother and the Grand General are plotting rebellion at the Third Month Shangsi festival feast; if it succeeds, they promise to make the sovereign Retired Emperor, the Grand General Heir Apparent, and the Guard General Grand Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I hear the Grand Younger Brother and the Grand General are plotting rebellion at the Third Month Shangsi festival feast. If it succeeds, they promise to make the sovereign Retired Emperor, the Grand General Heir Apparent, and the Guard General Grand Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 三王處不疑之地，並握重兵，以此舉事，無不成者。

translations.literal: The three princes occupy positions beyond suspicion and together hold heavy armies—to raise rebellion on this basis, nothing would fail.
translations.idiomatic: The three princes occupy positions beyond suspicion and together hold heavy armies. On that basis, rebellion could hardly fail.

sentences.zh: 然二王貪一時之利，不顧父兄，事成之後，主上豈有全理？

translations.literal: Yet the two princes, greedy for momentary gain and heedless of father and elder brother—once it succeeds, could the sovereign possibly survive intact?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two princes, greedy for momentary gain and heedless of father and elder brother—once it succeeds, could the sovereign possibly survive intact?

sentences.zh: 殿下兄弟，固不待言；

translations.literal: Your Highness and your brothers—need I say more;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness and your brothers—need I say more;

sentences.zh: 東宮、相國、單于，當在武陵兄弟，何肯與人也！

translations.literal: the Eastern Palace, the Chancellorship, and the Chanyu title would go to the brothers of Wuling—why would they give those to anyone else!
translations.idiomatic: the Eastern Palace, the Chancellorship, and the Chanyu title would go to the brothers of Wuling—why would they give those to anyone else!

sentences.zh: 今禍期甚迫，宜早圖之。

translations.literal: Now disaster is close at hand—you should plan early.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster is close at hand. You should plan early.

sentences.zh: 臣屢言於主上，主上篤於友愛，以臣刀鋸之餘，終不之信。

translations.literal: I have repeatedly spoken to the sovereign, but he is steeped in brotherly affection; considering me a man already under the knife and saw, he simply will not believe me.
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly spoken to the sovereign, but he is steeped in brotherly affection. Considering me a man already under the knife and saw, he simply will not believe me.

sentences.zh: 願殿下勿洩，密表其狀。

translations.literal: I beg Your Highness not to reveal this but secretly memorialize the facts.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness not to reveal this but secretly memorialize the facts.

sentences.zh: 殿下倘不信臣，可召大將軍從事中郎王皮、衛軍司馬劉惇，假之恩意，許其歸首以問之，必可知也。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness still does not believe me, you may summon the Grand General's Consultation Official Wang Pi and Guard General's Chief Clerk Liu Dun, treat them with kindness, promise them pardon if they confess, and question them—you will surely know the truth."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness still does not believe me, summon the Grand General's Consultation Official Wang Pi and Guard General's Chief Clerk Liu Dun. Treat them with kindness, promise them pardon if they confess, and question them—you will surely know the truth."

sentences.zh: 粲許之。

translations.literal: Zan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zan agreed.

sentences.zh: 猗密謂皮、惇曰：「二王逆狀，主上及相國具知之矣，卿同之乎？」

translations.literal: Yi secretly said to Pi and Dun: "The two princes' treasonous conduct—the sovereign and the Chancellor already know it all. Are you involved?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi secretly said to Pi and Dun, "The two princes' treason—the sovereign and the Chancellor already know it all. Are you involved?"

sentences.zh: 二人驚曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: The two men said in alarm: "We are not."
translations.idiomatic: The two men said in alarm, "We are not."

sentences.zh: 猗曰：「茲事已決，吾憐卿親舊並見族耳！」

translations.literal: Yi said: "This affair is already decided. I pity you and your kin—you will all be exterminated!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "This affair is already decided. I pity you and your kin—you will all be exterminated!"

sentences.zh: 因歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: and he sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: And he sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 二人大懼，叩頭求哀。

translations.literal: The two men were greatly afraid and kowtowed begging for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were terrified and kowtowed begging for mercy.

sentences.zh: 猗曰：「吾為卿計，卿能用之乎？

translations.literal: Yi said: "I have a plan for you—will you use it?
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "I have a plan for you—will you use it?

sentences.zh: 相國問卿，卿但云『有之』；

translations.literal: When the Chancellor questions you, you need only say 'We were involved';
translations.idiomatic: When the Chancellor questions you, say only, 'We were involved.'

sentences.zh: 若責卿不先啟，卿即云『臣誠負死罪。

translations.literal: if he reproaches you for not reporting it first, say 'I truly deserve death.
translations.idiomatic: If he reproaches you for not reporting it first, say, 'I truly deserve death.

sentences.zh: 然仰惟主上寬仁，殿下敦睦，苟言不見信，則陷於誣譖不測之誅，故不敢言也。』」

translations.literal: Yet considering the sovereign's generosity and Your Highness's kindness, if my words were not believed I would fall under unpredictable punishment for false accusation—so I dared not speak.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yet considering the sovereign's generosity and Your Highness's kindness, if my words were not believed I would fall under unpredictable punishment for false accusation—so I dared not speak.'"

sentences.zh: 皮、惇許諾。

translations.literal: Pi and Dun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Pi and Dun agreed.

sentences.zh: 粲召問之，二人至不同時，而其辭若一，粲以為信然。

translations.literal: Zan summoned and questioned them; though the two arrived at different times, their words matched as one—Zan believed it true.
translations.idiomatic: Zan summoned and questioned them. Though the two arrived at different times, their words matched exactly—Zan believed it.

sentences.zh: 勒准復說粲曰：「殿下宜自居東宮，以領相國，使天下早有所繫。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun again urged Zan, saying: "Your Highness ought to take the Eastern Palace for yourself and thus head the Chancellorship, so that all under Heaven may soon have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun again urged Zan, saying, "Your Highness ought to take the Eastern Palace for yourself and thus head the Chancellorship, so that all under Heaven may soon have something to rely on.

sentences.zh: 今道路之言，皆雲大將軍、衛將軍欲奉太弟為變，期以季春；

translations.literal: Now talk on the roads all says the Grand General and Guard General wish to install the Grand Younger Brother in rebellion, timed for late spring;
translations.idiomatic: Now talk on the roads all says the Grand General and Guard General wish to install the Grand Younger Brother in rebellion, timed for late spring;

sentences.zh: 若使太弟得天下，殿下無容足之地矣。」

translations.literal: if the Grand Younger Brother gets the empire, Your Highness will have nowhere to stand."
translations.idiomatic: if the Grand Younger Brother gets the empire, Your Highness will have nowhere to stand."

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「為之奈何？」

translations.literal: Zan said: "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Zan said, "What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 准曰：「人告太弟為變，主上必不信。

translations.literal: Zhun said: "If someone reports the Grand Younger Brother's rebellion, the sovereign will surely not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun said, "If someone reports the Grand Younger Brother's rebellion, the sovereign will surely not believe it.

sentences.zh: 宜緩東宮之禁，使賓客得往來；

translations.literal: You should relax restrictions on the Eastern Palace so guests may come and go;
translations.idiomatic: Relax restrictions on the Eastern Palace so guests may come and go;

sentences.zh: 太弟雅好待士，必不以此為嫌，輕薄小人不能無迎合太弟之意為之謀者。

translations.literal: the Grand Younger Brother has always loved treating scholars well—he will surely not object; but frivolous petty men cannot fail to seek to please him and plot on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Younger Brother has always loved treating scholars well—he will surely not object. But frivolous petty men cannot fail to seek to please him and plot on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 然後下官為殿下露表其罪，殿下收其賓客與太弟交通者考問之，獄辭既具，則主上無不信之理也。」

translations.literal: Then I will publicly memorialize his crimes for Your Highness; Your Highness can seize the guests who consort with the Eastern Palace and interrogate them—once the case is complete, the sovereign will have no reason not to believe."
translations.idiomatic: Then I will publicly memorialize his crimes for Your Highness. Seize the guests who consort with the Eastern Palace and interrogate them—once the case is complete, the sovereign will have no reason not to believe."

sentences.zh: 粲乃命卜抽引兵去東宮。

translations.literal: Zan then ordered Bu Chou to withdraw troops from the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zan then ordered Bu Chou to withdraw troops from the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 少府陳休、左衛將軍卜崇，為人清直，素惡沈等，雖在公座，未嘗與語，沈等深疾之。

translations.literal: Minister of the Imperial Household Chen Xiu and Left Guard General Bu Chong were upright men who had long hated Shen and the others; even in public assembly they never spoke with them—Shen and the others deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Imperial Household Chen Xiu and Left Guard General Bu Chong were upright men who had long hated Shen and the others. Even in public assembly they never spoke with them—Shen and the others deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 侍中卜干謂休、崇曰：「王沈等勢力足以回天地，卿輩自料親賢孰與竇武、陳蕃？」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Bu Gan said to Xiu and Chong: "Wang Shen and the others have power enough to overturn heaven and earth—do you measure yourselves against Dou Wu and Chen Fan in closeness to the worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Bu Gan said to Xiu and Chong, "Wang Shen and the others have power enough to overturn heaven and earth. Do you measure yourselves against Dou Wu and Chen Fan in closeness to the throne?"

sentences.zh: 休、崇曰：「吾輩年逾五十，職位已崇，唯欠一死耳！

translations.literal: Xiu and Chong said: "We are already past fifty, our offices already high—we lack only death!
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and Chong said, "We are already past fifty, our offices already high—we lack only death!

sentences.zh: 死於忠義，乃為得所；

translations.literal: To die for loyalty and righteousness is to die in the right place;
translations.idiomatic: To die for loyalty and righteousness is to die in the right place;

sentences.zh: 安能俛首低眉以事閹豎乎！

translations.literal: how could we bow our heads and knit our brows to serve eunuch minions!
translations.idiomatic: how could we bow our heads and knit our brows to serve eunuch minions!

sentences.zh: 去矣卜公，勿復有言！」

translations.literal: Go, Lord Bu—say no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Go, Lord Bu—say no more!"

sentences.zh: 二月，漢主聰出臨上秋閣，命收陳休、卜崇及特進綦毋達、太中大夫公彧、尚書王琰、田歆、大司農朱諧並誅之，皆宦官所惡也。

translations.literal: In the second month, Han Sovereign Cong came out to the Shangqiu Pavilion and ordered the arrest of Chen Xiu, Bu Chong, Special Advisor Qimu Da, Palace Counselor Gong Yu, Secretaries Wang Yan, Tian Xin, and Minister of Finance Zhu Xie—all executed; all were hated by the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Han Sovereign Liu Cong came out to the Shangqiu Pavilion and ordered the arrest of Chen Xiu, Bu Chong, Special Advisor Qimu Da, Palace Counselor Gong Yu, Secretaries Wang Yan and Tian Xin, and Minister of Finance Zhu Xie—all executed. All were hated by the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 卜干泣諫曰：「陛下方側席求賢，而一旦戮卿大夫七人，皆國之忠良，無乃不可乎！

translations.literal: Bu Gan remonstrated through tears: "Your Majesty has just begun to seek worthy men with an empty seat—yet in one stroke you slay seven ministers and great officers, all loyal pillars of the state. Surely this cannot be right!
translations.idiomatic: Bu Gan remonstrated through tears, "Your Majesty has just begun to seek worthy men with an empty seat—yet in one stroke you slay seven ministers and great officers, all loyal pillars of the state. Surely this cannot be right!

sentences.zh: 藉使休等有罪，陛下不下之有司，暴明其狀，天下何從知之！

translations.literal: Even if Xiu and the others were guilty, if Your Majesty does not turn them over to the proper offices and openly establish their crimes, how would all under Heaven know!
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xiu and the others were guilty, if Your Majesty does not turn them over to the proper offices and openly establish their crimes, how would all under Heaven know?

sentences.zh: 詔尚在臣所，未敢宣露，願陛下熟思之！」

translations.literal: The edict is still in my possession—I have not dared publish it. I beg Your Majesty to think this through carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: The edict is still in my possession—I have not dared publish it. I beg Your Majesty to think this through carefully!"

sentences.zh: 因叩頭流血。

translations.literal: and he kowtowed until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 王沈叱干曰：「卜侍中欲拒詔乎！」

translations.literal: Wang Shen shouted at Gan: "Does Palace Attendant Bu wish to resist the edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen shouted at Gan, "Does Palace Attendant Bu wish to resist the edict?"

sentences.zh: 聰拂衣而入，免干為庶人。

translations.literal: Cong brushed his robes and went inside, demoting Gan to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Cong brushed his robes and went inside, demoting Gan to commoner.

sentences.zh: 太宰河間王易、大將軍勃海王敷、御史大夫陳元達、金紫光祿大夫西河王延等皆詣闕表諫曰：「王沈等矯弄詔旨，欺誣日月，內諂陛下，外佞相國，威權之重，侔於人主，多樹奸黨，毒流海內。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Prince of Hejian Yi, Grand General Prince of Bohai Fu, Censor-in-Chief Chen Yuanda, Grandee of Splendid Happiness Prince of Xihe Yan, and others all came to the gate with memorials remonstrating: "Wang Shen and the others forge and twist imperial edicts, deceiving heaven and earth—flattering Your Majesty within while fawning on the Chancellor without. Their authority rivals the sovereign's; they have planted many villainous factions whose poison spreads across the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Prince of Hejian Liu Yi, Grand General Prince of Bohai Liu Fu, Censor-in-Chief Chen Yuanda, Grandee of Splendid Happiness Prince of Xihe Liu Yan, and others all came to the gate with memorials remonstrating: "Wang Shen and the others forge and twist imperial edicts, deceiving heaven and earth—flattering Your Majesty within while fawning on the Chancellor without. Their authority rivals the sovereign's. They have planted many villainous factions whose poison spreads across the seas.

sentences.zh: 知休等忠臣，為國盡節，恐發其奸狀，故巧為誣陷。

translations.literal: Knowing that Xiu and the others were loyal ministers who gave their all for the state, fearing exposure of their own villainy, they craftily framed false charges.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Xiu and the others were loyal ministers who gave their all for the state, and fearing exposure of their own villainy, they craftily framed false charges.

sentences.zh: 陛下不察，遽加極刑，痛徹天地，賢愚傷懼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, failing to discern this, hastily imposed extreme punishment—pain piercing heaven and earth, the worthy and the simple alike stricken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, failing to discern this, hastily imposed extreme punishment—pain piercing heaven and earth, the worthy and the simple alike stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 今遺晉未殄，巴、蜀不賓，石勒謀據趙、魏，曹嶷欲王全齊，陛下心腹四支，何處無患！

translations.literal: Now the remnant Jin is not yet destroyed, Ba and Shu have not submitted, Shi Le plots to hold Zhao and Wei, Cao Yi wishes to rule all Qi—at the heart and limbs of Your Majesty's body, where is there no peril!
translations.idiomatic: Now the remnant Jin is not yet destroyed, Ba and Shu have not submitted, Shi Le plots to hold Zhao and Wei, and Cao Yi wishes to rule all Qi—at the heart and limbs of Your Majesty's body, where is there no peril!

sentences.zh: 乃復以沈等助亂，誅巫咸，戮扁鵲，臣恐遂成膏盲之疾，後雖救之，不可及已。

translations.literal: Yet you again employ Shen and the others to aid disorder—executing Wu Xian and killing Bian Que. I fear you will end with an illness beyond remedy; though you may try to cure it later, it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you again employ Shen and the others to aid disorder—executing Wu Xian and killing Bian Que. I fear you will end with an illness beyond remedy; though you may try to cure it later, it will be too late.

sentences.zh: 請免沈等官，付有司治罪。」

translations.literal: We beg that Shen and the others be dismissed from office and handed to the proper authorities for punishment."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that Shen and the others be dismissed from office and handed to the proper authorities for punishment."

sentences.zh: 聰以表示沈等，笑曰：「群兒為元達所引，遂成癡也。」

translations.literal: Cong showed the memorial to Shen and the others and laughed: "These boys, led astray by Yuanda, have become fools."
translations.idiomatic: Cong showed the memorial to Shen and the others and laughed, "These boys, led astray by Yuanda, have become fools."

sentences.zh: 沈等頓首泣曰：「臣等小人，過蒙陛下識拔，得灑掃閨閣；

translations.literal: Shen and the others kowtowed weeping: "We petty men have unduly received Your Majesty's recognition and elevation, granted the honor of sweeping the inner chambers;
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the others kowtowed weeping, "We petty men have unduly received Your Majesty's recognition and elevation, granted the honor of sweeping the inner chambers;

sentences.zh: 而王公、朝士疾臣等如仇，又深恨陛下。

translations.literal: yet the princes and court gentlemen hate us as enemies and deeply resent Your Majesty as well.
translations.idiomatic: yet the princes and court gentlemen hate us as enemies and deeply resent Your Majesty as well.

sentences.zh: 願以臣等膏鼎鑊，則朝廷自然雍穆矣。」

translations.literal: We wish to be boiled in cauldrons—then the court would naturally be harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: We wish to be boiled in cauldrons—then the court would naturally be harmonious."

sentences.zh: 聰曰：「此等狂言常然，卿何足恨乎！」

translations.literal: Cong said: "Such mad talk is always happening—why should you resent it!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "Such mad talk is always happening—why should you resent it?"

sentences.zh: 聰問沈等於相國粲，粲盛稱沈等忠清；

translations.literal: Cong asked Chancellor Zan about Shen and the others; Zan highly praised them as loyal and pure;
translations.idiomatic: Cong asked Chancellor Liu Zan about Shen and the others. Zan highly praised them as loyal and pure;

sentences.zh: 聰悅，封沈等為列候。

translations.literal: Cong was pleased and enfeoffed Shen and the others as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was pleased and enfeoffed Shen and the others as ranked marquises.

sentences.zh: 太宰易又詣闕上疏極諫，聰大怒，手壞其疏。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yi again came to the gate with a memorial of fierce remonstrance; Cong was furious and tore the memorial apart with his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Liu Yi again came to the gate with a memorial of fierce remonstrance. Cong was furious and tore the memorial apart with his hands.

sentences.zh: 三月，易忿恚而卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yi died of rage and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Yi died of rage and indignation.

sentences.zh: 易素忠直，陳元達倚之為援，得盡諫諍。

translations.literal: Yi had always been loyal and upright; Chen Yuanda had relied on him as support and so was able to remonstrate to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had always been loyal and upright. Chen Yuanda had relied on him as support and so was able to remonstrate to the full.

sentences.zh: 及卒，元達哭之慟，曰：「『人之雲亡，邦國殄悴。』

translations.literal: When he died, Yuanda mourned him bitterly and said: "'When good men perish, the state is laid waste.'
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Yuanda mourned him bitterly and said, "'When good men perish, the state is laid waste.'

sentences.zh: 吾既不復能言，安用默默苟生乎！」

translations.literal: I can no longer speak out—what use is it to live on in silent submission!"
translations.idiomatic: I can no longer speak out—what use is it to live on in silent submission!"

sentences.zh: 歸而自殺。

translations.literal: He returned home and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 初，代王猗盧愛其少子比延，欲以為嗣，使長子六修出居新平城，而黜其母。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Dai Tuoba Yilu favored his younger son Biyan and wished to make him heir; he sent his eldest son Liuxiu to live at Xincheng and deposed Liuxiu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tuoba Yilu, Prince of Dai, favored his younger son Biyan and wished to make him heir. He sent his eldest son Liuxiu to live at Xincheng and deposed Liuxiu's mother.

sentences.zh: 六修有駿馬，日行五百里，猗盧奪之，以與比延。

translations.literal: Liuxiu had a fine horse that could run five hundred li in a day; Yilu seized it and gave it to Biyan.
translations.idiomatic: Liuxiu owned a fine horse that could run five hundred li in a day. Yilu seized it and gave it to Biyan.

sentences.zh: 六修來朝，猗盧使拜比延，六修不從。

translations.literal: Liuxiu came to court; Yilu had him bow to Biyan, and Liuxiu refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Liuxiu came to court, Yilu ordered him to bow to Biyan. Liuxiu refused.

sentences.zh: 猗盧乃坐比延於其步輦，使人導從出遊。

translations.literal: Yilu then seated Biyan on his palanquin and had attendants escort him out on an excursion.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu then seated Biyan on his own palanquin and sent attendants to escort him on an outing.

sentences.zh: 六修望見，以為猗盧，伏謁路左；

translations.literal: Liuxiu saw them from afar, thought it was Yilu, and prostrated himself by the roadside to pay respects;
translations.idiomatic: Liuxiu saw them from afar, thought it was Yilu, and prostrated himself by the roadside to pay his respects;

sentences.zh: 至，乃比延，六修慚怒而去。

translations.literal: when they arrived it was Biyan; ashamed and enraged, Liuxiu left.
translations.idiomatic: when they arrived it was Biyan. Ashamed and enraged, Liuxiu left.

sentences.zh: 猗盧召之不至，大怒，帥眾討之，為六修所敗。

translations.literal: Yilu summoned him but he did not come; furious, Yilu led troops to attack him and was defeated by Liuxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu summoned him, but he would not come. Furious, Yilu led troops against him and was defeated by Liuxiu.

sentences.zh: 猗盧微服逃民間，有賤婦人識之，遂為六修所弒。

translations.literal: Yilu fled in disguise among the people; a lowborn woman recognized him, and he was then assassinated by Liuxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu fled in disguise among the common people. A lowborn woman recognized him, and Liuxiu had him assassinated.

sentences.zh: 拓跋普根先守外境，聞難來赴，攻六修，滅之。

translations.literal: Tuoba Pugen, who had been guarding the frontier, heard of the crisis and came; he attacked Liuxiu and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Pugen, who had been guarding the frontier, heard of the crisis and came to help. He attacked Liuxiu and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 普根代立，國中大亂，新舊猜嫌，迭相誅滅。

translations.literal: Pugen succeeded to the throne; great disorder arose in the state; old and new factions suspected one another and slaughtered one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Pugen succeeded to the throne. The state fell into great disorder; old and new factions suspected one another and slaughtered one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 左將軍衛雄、信義將軍箕澹，久佐猗盧，為眾所附，謀歸劉琨，乃言於眾曰：「聞舊人忌新人悍戰，欲盡殺之，將奈何？」

translations.literal: Left General Wei Xiong and Faithful Righteousness General Ji Dan, long Yilu's lieutenants and well regarded by the people, planned to go over to Liu Kun and said to the assembly: "We hear the old settlers envy the new arrivals' fierceness in battle and wish to kill them all—what are we to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Left General Wei Xiong and Faithful Righteousness General Ji Dan, who had long served Yilu and were well regarded, planned to go over to Liu Kun. They said to the assembly, "We hear the old settlers envy the new arrivals' fierceness in battle and wish to kill them all. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 晉人及烏桓皆驚懼，曰：「死生隨二將軍！」

translations.literal: The Jin people and Wuhuan were all alarmed and said: "Life and death follow the two generals!"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin people and Wuhuan were all alarmed and said, "Life and death follow the two generals!"

sentences.zh: 乃與琨質子遵帥晉人及烏桓三萬家、馬牛羊十萬頭歸於琨。

translations.literal: They then, with Kun's hostage son Zun, led thirty thousand Jin and Wuhuan households and a hundred thousand head of horses, cattle, and sheep to join Kun.
translations.idiomatic: They then, with Kun's hostage son Zun, led thirty thousand Jin and Wuhuan households and a hundred thousand head of horses, cattle, and sheep to join Kun.

sentences.zh: 琨大喜，親詣平城撫納之，琨兵由是復振。

translations.literal: Kun was greatly pleased, went in person to Pingcheng to receive and settle them, and Kun's forces were thereby revived.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was greatly pleased. He went in person to Pingcheng to receive and settle them, and his forces were thereby revived.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，普根卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Pugen died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Pugen died.

sentences.zh: 其子始生，普根母惟氏立之。

translations.literal: His son had just been born; Pugen's mother Lady Wei installed him as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His son had just been born, and Pugen's mother, Lady Wei, installed him as ruler.

sentences.zh: 張實下令：所部吏民有能舉其過者，賞以布帛羊米。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi issued an order: any official or commoner under his command who could report his faults would be rewarded with cloth, silk, sheep, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi issued an order: any official or commoner under his command who reported his faults would be rewarded with cloth, silk, sheep, and grain.

sentences.zh: 賊曹佐高昌隗瑾曰：「今明公為政，事無鉅細，皆自決之，或興師發令，府朝不知；

translations.literal: Criminal Affairs Aide Wei Jin of Gaochang said: "Now Your Excellency governs—matters great and small you decide yourself; sometimes you raise armies and issue orders and the prefectural court knows nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Criminal Affairs Aide Wei Jin of Gaochang said, "Your Excellency now governs so that matters great and small are all decided by you alone. Sometimes you raise armies and issue orders, and the prefectural court knows nothing;

sentences.zh: 萬一違失，謗無所分。

translations.literal: should there be any mistake, blame has nowhere to fall.
translations.idiomatic: should anything go wrong, blame has nowhere to fall.

sentences.zh: 群下畏威，受成而已。

translations.literal: Your subordinates fear your authority and merely accept finished decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Your subordinates fear your authority and merely accept finished decisions.

sentences.zh: 如此，雖賞之千金，終不敢言也。

translations.literal: In such circumstances, though you reward a thousand in gold, in the end none dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: In such circumstances, even a reward of a thousand in gold will not make anyone speak in the end.

sentences.zh: 謂宜少損聰明，凡百政事，皆延訪群下，使各盡所懷，然後采而行之，則嘉言自至，何必賞也！」

translations.literal: I suggest you reduce somewhat your own cleverness; in all government affairs consult your subordinates, let each speak his mind fully, then choose and act on what is said—good counsel will come of itself; why need rewards?"
translations.idiomatic: I suggest you rely less on your own brilliance. In all government affairs, consult your subordinates and let each speak his mind fully; then choose and act on what is said. Good counsel will come of itself—why need rewards?"

sentences.zh: 實悅，從之，增瑾位三等。

translations.literal: Shi was pleased, followed the advice, and raised Jin three ranks in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was pleased, followed the advice, and raised Jin three ranks in office.

sentences.zh: 實遣將軍王該帥步騎五千入援長安，且送諸郡貢計。

translations.literal: Shi sent General Wang Gai with five thousand infantry and cavalry to reinforce Chang'an and also deliver the tribute accounts of the various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Shi sent General Wang Gai with five thousand infantry and cavalry to reinforce Chang'an and deliver the tribute accounts of the various commanderies.

sentences.zh: 詔拜實都督陝西諸軍事，以實弟茂為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shi Director-General of all military affairs west of Shan and made Shi's younger brother Mao Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shi Director-General of all military affairs west of Shan and made his younger brother Mao Governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 石勒使石虎攻劉演於廩丘，幽州刺史段匹磾使其弟文鴦救之；

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Shi Hu to attack Liu Yan at Lüqiu; Youzhou Inspector Duan Pidi sent his younger brother Wen Yang to rescue him;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Shi Hu to attack Liu Yan at Lüqiu. Youzhou Inspector Duan Pidi sent his younger brother Wen Yang to rescue him;

sentences.zh: 虎拔廩丘，演奔文鴦軍，虎獲演弟啟以歸。

translations.literal: Hu took Lüqiu; Yan fled to Wen Yang's army; Hu captured Yan's younger brother Qi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hu took Lüqiu. Yan fled to Wen Yang's army, and Hu captured Yan's younger brother Qi and returned.

sentences.zh: 寧州刺史王遜，嚴猛喜誅殺。

translations.literal: Ningzhou Inspector Wang Xun was harsh and fierce and loved executions.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhou Inspector Wang Xun was harsh and fierce and loved executions.

sentences.zh: 五月，平夷太守雷炤、平樂太守董霸帥三千餘家叛，降於成。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Pingyi Administrator Lei Zhao and Pingle Administrator Dong Ba led more than three thousand households in rebellion and surrendered to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Pingyi Administrator Lei Zhao and Pingle Administrator Dong Ba led more than three thousand households in rebellion and surrendered to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，漢大司馬曜圍北地太守麴昌，大都督麴允將步騎三萬救之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Han Grand Marshal Yao besieged Beidi Administrator Qu Chang; Grand Governor Qu Yun led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Han Grand Marshal Liu Yao besieged Beidi Administrator Qu Chang. Grand Governor Qu Yun led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 曜繞城縱火，煙起蔽天，使反間紿允曰：「郡城已陷，往無及也！」

translations.literal: Yao encircled the city and set fires; smoke rose to blot out the sky; he sent disinformation to deceive Yun, saying: "The prefectural city has already fallen—going will be too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao encircled the city and set fires until smoke blotted out the sky. He sent disinformation to deceive Yun, saying, "The prefectural city has already fallen—going will be too late!"

sentences.zh: 眾懼而潰。

translations.literal: The troops panicked and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 曜追敗允於磻石谷，允奔還靈武，曜遂取北地。

translations.literal: Yao pursued and defeated Yun at Panshi Valley; Yun fled back to Lingwu; Yao then took Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao pursued and defeated Yun at Panshi Valley. Yun fled back to Lingwu, and Yao then took Beidi.

sentences.zh: 允性仁厚，無威斷，喜以爵位悅人。

translations.literal: Yun was by nature benevolent and generous, lacked stern decisiveness, and liked to please people with titles and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was by nature benevolent and generous, lacked stern decisiveness, and liked to please people with titles and rank.

sentences.zh: 新平太守竺恢、始平太守楊像、扶風太守竺爽、安定太守焦嵩，皆領征、鎮，杖節，加侍中、常侍；

translations.literal: Xingping Administrator Zhu Hui, Shiping Administrator Yang Xiang, Fufeng Administrator Zhu Shuang, and Anding Administrator Jiao Song all held expeditionary and garrison commands, carried imperial staffs, and were additionally made Palace Attendants and Regular Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Xingping Administrator Zhu Hui, Shiping Administrator Yang Xiang, Fufeng Administrator Zhu Shuang, and Anding Administrator Jiao Song all held expeditionary and garrison commands, carried imperial staffs, and were additionally made Palace Attendants and Regular Attendants;

sentences.zh: 村塢主帥，小者猶假銀青將軍之號；

translations.literal: village stockade chiefs, even the minor ones, were granted titles such as General with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon;
translations.idiomatic: village stockade chiefs, even the minor ones, were granted titles such as General with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon;

sentences.zh: 然恩不及下，故諸將驕恣而士卒離怨。

translations.literal: yet his favor did not reach the lower ranks, so the generals were arrogant and willful while the soldiers grew discontented and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: yet his favor did not reach the lower ranks, so the generals grew arrogant and willful while the soldiers became discontented and resentful.

sentences.zh: 關中危亂，允告急於焦嵩；

translations.literal: Guanzhong was in peril; Yun urgently appealed to Jiao Song;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was in peril, and Yun urgently appealed to Jiao Song;

sentences.zh: 嵩素侮允，曰：「須允困，當救之。」

translations.literal: Song had always looked down on Yun and said: "Wait until Yun is trapped—we will rescue him then."
translations.idiomatic: Song had always looked down on Yun and said, "Wait until Yun is trapped—we will rescue him then."

sentences.zh: 曜進至涇陽，渭北諸城悉潰。

translations.literal: Yao advanced to Jingyang; all the cities north of the Wei collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao advanced to Jingyang, and all the cities north of the Wei collapsed.

sentences.zh: 曜獲建威將軍魯充、散騎常侍梁緯、少府皇甫陽。

translations.literal: Yao captured Establishing Might General Lu Chong, Regular Palace Attendant Liang Wei, and Chamberlain for the Palace Huangfu Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao captured Establishing Might General Lu Chong, Regular Palace Attendant Liang Wei, and Chamberlain for the Palace Huangfu Yang.

sentences.zh: 曜素聞充賢，募生致之，既見，賜之酒曰：「吾得子，天下不足定也！」

translations.literal: Yao had long heard Chong was worthy; he offered a reward to take him alive; once they met, he gave him wine and said: "With you in my service, securing the realm would be easy!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao had long heard that Chong was worthy and offered a reward to take him alive. Once they met, he gave him wine and said, "With you in my service, securing the realm would be easy!"

sentences.zh: 充曰：「身為晉將，國家喪敗，不敢求生。

translations.literal: Chong said: "As a Jin general, with the state ruined and defeated, I dare not seek to live.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "As a Jin general, with the state ruined and defeated, I dare not seek to live.

sentences.zh: 若蒙公恩，速死為幸。」

translations.literal: If I may receive your grace, a swift death would be good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: If I may receive your grace, a swift death would be good fortune."

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「義士也。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "A man of integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Yao said, "A man of integrity."

sentences.zh: 賜之劍，令自殺。

translations.literal: He gave him a sword and ordered him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him a sword and ordered him to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 梁緯妻辛氏，美色，曜召見，將妻之，辛氏大哭曰：「妾夫已死，義不獨生，且一婦人而事二夫，明公又安用之！」

translations.literal: Liang Wei's wife, Lady Xin, was beautiful; Yao summoned her and intended to marry her; Lady Xin wept loudly: "My husband is dead—I cannot in honor live alone; besides, what use would Your Excellency have for a woman who served two husbands!"
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wei's wife, Lady Xin, was beautiful. Yao summoned her and intended to marry her. Lady Xin wept loudly, "My husband is dead—I cannot in honor live alone. Besides, what use would Your Excellency have for a woman who served two husbands!"

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「貞女也。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "A chaste woman."
translations.idiomatic: Yao said, "A chaste woman."

sentences.zh: 亦聽自殺，皆以禮葬之。

translations.literal: He also permitted her to kill herself; both were buried with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also permitted her to kill herself. Both were buried with full rites.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰立故張後侍婢樊氏為上皇后，三後之外，佩皇后璽綬者復有七人。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong made former Empress Zhang's handmaid Fan Shi Grand Empress; apart from the three empresses, seven more women wore the empress seal and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong made former Empress Zhang's handmaid Fan Shi Grand Empress. Apart from the three empresses, seven more women wore the empress seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 嬖寵用事，刑賞紊亂。

translations.literal: Favored consorts held power; punishments and rewards were in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Favored consorts held power, and punishments and rewards fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 大將軍敷數涕泣切諫，聰怒曰：「汝欲乃公速死邪，何以朝夕生來哭人！」

translations.literal: Grand General Fu repeatedly remonstrated in tears; Cong angrily said: "Do you want your old man to die quickly—why do you come crying at me morning and night!"
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Fu repeatedly remonstrated in tears. Cong angrily said, "Do you want your old man to die quickly? Why do you come crying at me morning and night!"

sentences.zh: 敷憂憤，發病卒。

translations.literal: Fu died of grief and anger from the illness it caused.
translations.idiomatic: Fu died of grief and anger from the illness it caused.

sentences.zh: 河東平陽大蝗，民流殍者什五六。

translations.literal: Great locust swarms struck Pingyang in Hedong; five or six tenths of the people fled or starved.
translations.idiomatic: Great locust swarms struck Pingyang in Hedong. Five or six tenths of the people fled or starved.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣其將石越帥騎二萬屯并州，招納流民，民歸之者二十萬戶。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent his general Shi Yue with twenty thousand cavalry to encamp in Bingzhou and gather displaced people; two hundred thousand households returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent his general Shi Yue with twenty thousand cavalry to encamp in Bingzhou and gather displaced people. Two hundred thousand households returned to him.

sentences.zh: 聰遣使讓勒，勒不受命，潛與曹嶷相結。

translations.literal: Cong sent envoys to rebuke Shi Le; Le refused the order and secretly allied with Cao Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cong sent envoys to rebuke Shi Le. Le refused the order and secretly allied with Cao Yi.

sentences.zh: 八月，漢大司馬曜逼長安。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Han Grand Marshal Yao pressed Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Han Grand Marshal Liu Yao pressed Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 九月，漢主宴群臣於光極殿，引見太弟乂。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Han ruler entertained his ministers in the Hall of Grand Brilliance and summoned his younger brother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Han ruler entertained his ministers in the Hall of Grand Brilliance and summoned his younger brother Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 乂容貌憔悴，鬢髮蒼然，涕泣陳謝，聰亦為之慟哭；

translations.literal: Yi's appearance was haggard, his temples grey; weeping he expressed his remorse; Cong also wept bitterly for him;
translations.idiomatic: Yi's appearance was haggard and his temples grey. Weeping, he expressed his remorse, and Cong also wept bitterly for him;

sentences.zh: 乃縱酒極歡，待之如初。

translations.literal: they then drank freely in great merriment and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: they then drank freely in great merriment and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 焦嵩、竺恢、宋哲皆引兵救長安，散騎常侍華輯監京兆、馮翊、弘農、上洛四郡兵，屯霸上，皆畏漢兵強，不敢進。

translations.literal: Jiao Song, Zhu Hui, and Song Zhe all led troops to rescue Chang'an; Regular Palace Attendant Hua Ji supervised the forces of the four commanderies Jingzhao, Fufeng, Hongnong, and Shangluo, encamped at Bashang—all feared the Han armies' strength and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Song, Zhu Hui, and Song Zhe all led troops to rescue Chang'an. Regular Palace Attendant Hua Ji supervised the forces of the four commanderies Jingzhao, Fufeng, Hongnong, and Shangluo and encamped at Bashang. All feared the Han armies' strength and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 相國保遣胡崧將兵入援，擊漢大司馬曜於靈台，破之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Bao sent Hu Song with troops to reinforce; he attacked Han Grand Marshal Yao at Lingtai and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bao sent Hu Song with troops to reinforce Chang'an. He attacked Han Grand Marshal Liu Yao at Lingtai and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 崧恐國威復振則麴、索勢盛，乃帥城西諸郡兵屯渭北不進，遂還槐裡。

translations.literal: Song feared that if the state's prestige revived, Qu and Suo would grow too powerful; he led the western commandery troops to encamp north of the Wei without advancing, then returned to Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: Song feared that if the state's prestige revived, Qu and Suo would grow too powerful. He led the western commandery troops to encamp north of the Wei without advancing, then returned to Huaili.

sentences.zh: 曜攻陷長安外城，麴允、索綝退守小城以自固。

translations.literal: Yao stormed the outer wall of Chang'an; Qu Yun and Suo Jin withdrew to hold the inner city for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yao stormed the outer wall of Chang'an. Qu Yun and Suo Jin withdrew to hold the inner city for defense.

sentences.zh: 內外斷絕，城中饑甚，米斗直金二兩，人相食，死者太半，亡逃不可制，唯涼州義眾千人，守死不移。

translations.literal: Inside and outside were cut off; famine was severe in the city—a dou of rice cost two liang of gold; people ate one another; more than half died; desertions could not be controlled; only a thousand loyal volunteers from Liangzhou held firm to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside were cut off. Famine was severe in the city—a dou of rice cost two liang of gold. People ate one another; more than half died. Desertions could not be controlled. Only a thousand loyal volunteers from Liangzhou held firm to the death.

sentences.zh: 太倉有麴數十餅，麴允屑之為粥以供帝，既而亦盡。

translations.literal: The state granary had several dozen cakes of ferment; Qu Yun ground them into porridge to feed the emperor; soon these too were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The state granary had several dozen cakes of ferment. Qu Yun ground them into porridge to feed the emperor, and soon these too were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，帝泣謂允曰：「今窮厄如此，外無救援，當忍恥出降，以活士民。」

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, the emperor wept and said to Yun: "Now reduced to such extremity, with no rescue from outside—we should swallow our shame and surrender to save the officials and people."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, the emperor wept and said to Yun, "Now reduced to such extremity, with no rescue from outside—we should swallow our shame and surrender to save the officials and people."

sentences.zh: 因歎曰：「誤我事者，麴、索二公也！」

translations.literal: He sighed: "Those who ruined my cause were the two lords Qu and Suo!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Those who ruined my cause were the two lords Qu and Suo!"

sentences.zh: 使侍中宗敞送降箋於曜。

translations.literal: He sent Palace Attendant Zong Chang to deliver the surrender letter to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Attendant Zong Chang to deliver the surrender letter to Yao.

sentences.zh: 索綝潛留敝，使其子說曜曰：「今城中食猶足支一年，未易克也，若許綝以車騎、儀同、萬戶郡公者，請以城降。」

translations.literal: Suo Jin secretly detained Chang and sent his son to tell Yao: "Provisions in the city can still last a year—it is not easily taken; if you grant Jin the titles of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Marquis of a ten-thousand-household commandery, he will surrender the city."
translations.idiomatic: Suo Jin secretly detained Chang and sent his son to tell Yao, "Provisions in the city can still last a year—it is not easily taken. If you grant Jin the titles of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Marquis of a ten-thousand-household commandery, he will surrender the city."

sentences.zh: 曜斬而送之，曰：「帝王之師，以義行也。

translations.literal: Yao executed the messenger and sent the head back, saying: "An army of a true king acts by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yao executed the messenger and sent the head back, saying, "An army of a true king acts by righteousness.

sentences.zh: 孤將兵十五年，未嘗以詭計敗人，必窮兵極勢，然後取之。

translations.literal: I have led troops for fifteen years and never defeated an enemy by stratagem—I must bring all force to bear and only then take what I seek.
translations.idiomatic: I have led troops for fifteen years and never defeated an enemy by stratagem. I must bring all force to bear and only then take what I seek.

sentences.zh: 今索綝所言如此，天下之惡一也，輒相為戮之。

translations.literal: Now Suo Jin speaks thus—the world's wickedness is one; I hereby execute him on your behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Now Suo Jin speaks thus—the world's wickedness is one. I hereby execute him on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 若兵食審未盡者，便可勉強固守；

translations.literal: If your troops and provisions are truly not exhausted, you may of course hold on stubbornly;
translations.idiomatic: If your troops and provisions are truly not exhausted, you may of course hold on stubbornly;

sentences.zh: 如其糧竭兵微，亦宜早寤天命。」

translations.literal: but if grain is gone and troops few, you should also awaken early to Heaven's decree."
translations.idiomatic: but if grain is gone and troops few, you should also awaken early to Heaven's decree."

sentences.zh: 甲午，宗敞至曜營；

translations.literal: On jiawu, Zong Chang reached Yao's camp;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu, Zong Chang reached Yao's camp;

sentences.zh: 乙未，帝乘羊車，肉袒、銜璧、輿櫬出東門降。

translations.literal: on yiwei, the emperor rode in a sheep cart, bared his upper body, held a jade disk in his mouth, and had a coffin carried before him as he went out the east gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiwei, the emperor rode in a sheep cart, bared his upper body, held a jade disk in his mouth, and had a coffin carried before him as he went out the east gate to surrender.

sentences.zh: 群臣號泣，攀車執帝手，帝亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: The ministers wailed; they clung to the cart and grasped the emperor's hand; the emperor too was overwhelmed with grief.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers wailed. They clung to the cart and grasped the emperor's hand, and the emperor too was overwhelmed with grief.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞馮翊吉朗歎曰：「吾智不能謀，勇不能死，何忍君臣相隨，北面事賊虜乎！」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Ji Lang of Fufeng sighed: "My wisdom could not devise a plan, my courage could not face death—how can I bear to follow my ruler and lord in bowing north to serve bandit invaders!"
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Ji Lang of Fufeng sighed, "My wisdom could not devise a plan, my courage could not face death—how can I bear to follow my ruler and lord in bowing north to serve bandit invaders!"

sentences.zh: 乃自殺。

translations.literal: He then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 曜焚櫬受璧，使宗敞奉帝還宮。

translations.literal: Yao burned the coffin and accepted the jade disk; he had Zong Chang escort the emperor back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yao burned the coffin and accepted the jade disk. He had Zong Chang escort the emperor back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，遷帝及公卿以下於其營；

translations.literal: On dingyou, he moved the emperor and the officials below him to his camp;
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, he moved the emperor and the officials below him to his camp;

sentences.zh: 辛丑，送至平陽。

translations.literal: on xinchou, he sent them to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou, he sent them to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，漢主聰臨光極殿，帝稽首於前。

translations.literal: On renyin, Han ruler Cong sat in the Hall of Grand Brilliance; the emperor kowtowed before him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, Han ruler Liu Cong sat in the Hall of Grand Brilliance, and the emperor kowtowed before him.

sentences.zh: 麴允伏地慟哭，扶不能起。

translations.literal: Qu Yun prostrated himself and wept bitterly; when helped up he could not stand.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun prostrated himself and wept bitterly. When helped up, he could not stand.

sentences.zh: 聰怒，囚之，允自殺。

translations.literal: Cong was angry and imprisoned him; Yun killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was angry and imprisoned him. Yun killed himself.

sentences.zh: 聰以帝為光祿大夫，封懷安候。

translations.literal: Cong made the emperor Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Cong made the emperor Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 以大司馬曜為假黃鉞、大都督、督陝西諸軍事、太宰，封秦王。

translations.literal: He made Grand Marshal Yao Acting Bearer of the Yellow Axe, Grand Governor, Director-General of all military affairs west of Shan, Grand Minister, and enfeoffed him as King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He made Grand Marshal Liu Yao Acting Bearer of the Yellow Axe, Grand Governor, Director-General of all military affairs west of Shan, Grand Minister, and enfeoffed him as King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元麟嘉。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Linjia.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Linjia.

sentences.zh: 以麴允忠烈，贈車騎將軍，謚節愍候。

translations.literal: Because Qu Yun was loyal and steadfast, he was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the posthumous title Marquis of Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qu Yun was loyal and steadfast, he was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the posthumous title Marquis of Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 以索綝不忠，斬於都市。

translations.literal: Because Suo Jin was disloyal, he was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Because Suo Jin was disloyal, he was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 尚書梁允、侍中梁浚等及諸郡守皆為曜所殺，華輯奔南山。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Liang Yun, Palace Attendant Liang Jun, and various commandery administrators were all killed by Yao; Hua Ji fled to the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Liang Yun, Palace Attendant Liang Jun, and various commandery administrators were all killed by Yao. Hua Ji fled to the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 干寶論曰：「昔高祖宣皇帝，以雄才碩量，應時而起，性深阻有若城府，而能寬綽以容納；

translations.literal: Gan Bao's commentary says: "Of old the High Ancestor, Emperor Xuan, with heroic talent and vast capacity, rose in response to the times; his nature was deep and guarded like hidden fortifications, yet he could be generous and accommodating;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's commentary says, "Of old the High Ancestor, Emperor Xuan, with heroic talent and vast capacity, rose in response to the times. His nature was deep and guarded like hidden fortifications, yet he could be generous and accommodating;

sentences.zh: 行數術以御物，而知人善采拔。

translations.literal: he practiced arts of calculation to control affairs and knew men well, excelling at selection and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: he practiced arts of calculation to control affairs and knew men well, excelling at selection and promotion.

sentences.zh: 於是百姓與能，大象始構。

translations.literal: Thus the people contributed their abilities and the great enterprise was first framed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people contributed their abilities and the great enterprise was first framed.

sentences.zh: 世宗承基，太祖繼業，鹹黜異圖，用融前烈。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor inherited the foundation, the Grand Ancestor continued the enterprise; both subdued rival designs and drew upon the achievements of their predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor inherited the foundation, and the Grand Ancestor continued the enterprise. Both subdued rival designs and drew upon the achievements of their predecessors.

sentences.zh: 至於世祖，遂享皇極，仁以厚下，儉以足用，和而不弛，寬而能斷，掩唐、虞之舊域，班正朔於八荒，於時有「天下無窮人」之諺，雖太平未洽，亦足以明民樂其生矣。

translations.literal: As for the Founding Emperor, he then ascended the imperial throne: benevolent in enriching the people below, frugal in sufficing for use, harmonious without slackening, broad yet able to decide—covering the old domains of Tang and Yu, extending the calendar to the eight wilds; at the time there was the proverb "Under Heaven there are no destitute men." Though perfect peace was not yet attained, it was enough to show that the people rejoiced in their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor came to the throne, he ruled with benevolence toward the people and frugality in state expenditure—harmonious without laxity, magnanimous yet decisive.
