He recovered the ancient domains of Tang and Yu and extended the imperial calendar to the farthest reaches of the realm. People said then that "there are no destitute men under Heaven." Though true peace had not yet been fully achieved, it was already clear that the people were content with their lives.

sentences.zh: 武皇既崩，山陵未干而變難繼起。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu died, before his tomb was dry calamities arose in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had Emperor Wu been buried when disaster followed disaster.

sentences.zh: 宗子無維城之助，師尹無具瞻之貴，朝為伊、周，夕成桀、跖；

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen gave no aid as bulwark cities; chief ministers lacked the dignity of universal regard—morning they were Yi and Zhou, evening they became Jie and Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: Royal princes offered no support as bulwarks of the throne; chief ministers commanded no universal respect—one morning they were Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, by evening they were Jie and Robber Zhi.

sentences.zh: 國政迭移於亂人，禁兵外散於四方，方岳無鈞石之鎮，關門無結草之固。

translations.literal: State affairs passed in turn to disorderly men; forbidden troops were scattered abroad to the four quarters; regional governors had no counterweight's weight to stabilize them; frontier passes had no knotting-grass firmness.
translations.idiomatic: State power passed from one schemer to the next; the imperial guard was dispersed across the realm; regional governors wielded no stabilizing weight; the frontier passes stood with no loyal defense.

sentences.zh: 戎、羯稱制，二帝失尊，何哉？

translations.literal: Rong and Jie seized power; the two emperors lost their dignity—why?
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian chieftains seized real power, and two emperors lost all dignity. How did it come to this?

sentences.zh: 樹立失權，托付非才，四維不張，而苟且之政多也。

translations.literal: Establishment lost its authority, entrustment fell to unworthy men, the four bonds were not stretched taut, and expedient government was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Those placed in power were given the wrong authority; responsibility was entrusted to the wrong men; the four bonds of the state were left slack; and makeshift, opportunist government became the rule.

sentences.zh: 夫基廣則難傾，根深則難拔，理節則不亂，膠結則不遷。

translations.literal: When the foundation is broad it is hard to overturn; when the roots are deep they are hard to uproot; when principle and order are clear there is no disorder; when bonds are glued firm there is no shifting.
translations.idiomatic: A broad foundation is hard to overturn; deep roots are hard to uproot; clear principle and order prevent chaos; firm bonds keep a state from drifting.

sentences.zh: 昔之有天下者所以能長久，用此道也。

translations.literal: Those who formerly possessed All Under Heaven could endure long because they used this Way.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasties that endured did so because they followed this principle.

sentences.zh: 周自後稷愛民，十六王而武始君之，其積基樹本，如此其固。

translations.literal: Zhou, from Hou Ji's love of the people, through sixteen kings until Wu first became ruler—their accumulation of foundation and planting of roots was as firm as this.
translations.idiomatic: From Hou Ji's care for the people down through sixteen kings until King Wu first took the throne, Zhou accumulated its foundation and planted its roots with just such solidity.

sentences.zh: 今晉之興也，其創基立本，固異於先代矣。

translations.literal: Now Jin's rise—its founding and establishment of roots—was fundamentally different from earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin rose to power, the way it laid its foundations was fundamentally unlike that of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 加以朝寡純德之人，鄉乏不二之老，風俗淫僻，恥尚失所。

translations.literal: Added to this, the court had few men of pure virtue; the villages lacked elders of undivided loyalty; customs were dissolute and perverse, and shame and esteem were misplaced.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the court had few men of genuine virtue, and the countryside few elders of unquestioned loyalty. Morals had turned dissolute and perverse; what people honored and what they shamed were all out of place.

sentences.zh: 學者以莊、老為宗而黜《六經》，談者以虛蕩為辯而賤名檢，行身者以放濁為通而狹節信，進仕者以苟得為貴而鄙居正，當官者以望空為高而笑勤恪。

translations.literal: Scholars took Zhuangzi and Laozi as their masters and dismissed the Six Classics; debaters took empty extravagance as eloquence and despised moral propriety; those conducting themselves took reckless license as openness and narrowed integrity and faithfulness; those entering office took opportunistic gain as noble and scorned upright conduct; officials took vacant indifference as loftiness and laughed at diligence and conscientiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars made Zhuangzi and Laozi their masters and set aside the Six Classics. Talkers prized empty cleverness over real argument and looked down on moral restraint. Men of the world treated reckless indulgence as sophistication and treated integrity as narrow-mindedness. Office-seekers valued easy gain and despised honest conduct. Officials treated idle detachment as refinement and mocked diligence and conscientiousness.

sentences.zh: 是以劉頌屢言治道，傅鹹每糾邪正，皆謂之俗吏；

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Song repeatedly spoke of the Way of governance, and Fu Xian constantly corrected wrong from right—both were called vulgar officials;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song repeatedly expounded the principles of good government, and Fu Xian constantly distinguished right from wrong—both were dismissed as vulgar bureaucrats.

sentences.zh: 其倚杖虛曠，依阿無心者，皆名重海內。

translations.literal: while those who leaned on empty vastness and fawned without conviction were all famed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile those who leaned on airy abstractions and fawned without conviction were all celebrated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 若夫文王日昃不暇食，仲山甫夙夜匪懈者，蓋共嗤黜以為灰塵矣！

translations.literal: As for King Wen, who worked until sunset without time to eat, and Zhong Shanfu, who never slackened day or night—they were all mocked and cast aside as dust!
translations.idiomatic: King Wen, who worked until sunset without time to eat, and Zhong Shanfu, who never slackened day or night—these men were mocked and cast aside like worthless dust!

sentences.zh: 由是毀譽亂於善惡之實，情慝奔於貨欲之塗，選者為人擇官，官者為身擇利，世族貴戚之子弟，陵邁超越，不拘資次。

translations.literal: From this praise and blame were confused with the reality of good and evil; private desires rushed toward the path of profit and goods; selectors chose offices for men, and officials chose profit for themselves; sons and younger brothers of noble clans and imperial kin vaulted over others without regard for seniority.
translations.idiomatic: From this, reputation and disgrace no longer matched real good and evil; private greed drove men toward profit; those who selected officials chose posts for their favorites, and officials chose posts for their own gain. Sons and younger brothers of great clans and imperial kin vaulted ahead without regard for rank or seniority.

sentences.zh: 悠悠風塵，皆奔競之士；

translations.literal: Through the drifting dust of the age, all were men racing in competition;
translations.idiomatic: In that restless age, every man was scrambling for advantage.

sentences.zh: 列官千百，無讓賢之舉。

translations.literal: Among hundreds and thousands of officials, there was no act of yielding place to the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Among hundreds and thousands of officials, not one stepped aside for a better man.

sentences.zh: 子真著《崇讓》而莫之省，子雅制九班而不得用。

translations.literal: Bo Chen wrote "On Honoring Yielding" and no one heeded it; Lu Ji devised the nine ranks and could not get it adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Chen wrote "On Honoring Yielding," and no one paid attention. Lu Ji devised the nine-rank system, and it could not be put into use.

sentences.zh: 其婦女不知女工，任情而動，有逆於舅姑，有殺戮妾媵，父兄弗之罪也，天下莫之非也。

translations.literal: Their women did not know women's work; acting on whim, some defied mothers-in-law, some killed concubines and secondary wives—fathers and elder brothers did not punish them, and none under Heaven blamed them.
translations.idiomatic: Their women knew nothing of women's work. Acting on whim, some defied their mothers-in-law; some killed concubines and secondary wives. Fathers and elder brothers did not punish them, and no one under Heaven thought it wrong.

sentences.zh: 禮法刑政，於此大壞。

translations.literal: Rites, law, punishments, and government—here they were greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual, law, punishment, and government were ruined on every side.

sentences.zh: 「國之將亡，本必先顛，」其此之謂乎！

translations.literal: "When a state is about to perish, its foundation must first topple"—is this not what is meant!"
translations.idiomatic: "When a state is about to perish, its foundation must first collapse"—surely this is what that saying means!"

sentences.zh: 故觀阮籍之行而覺禮教崩弛之所由，察庾純、賈充之爭而見師尹之多僻，考平吳之功而知將帥之不讓，思郭欽之謀而寤戎狄之有釁，覽傅玄、劉毅之言而得百官之邪，核傅鹹之奏、《錢神》之論而睹寵賂之彰。

translations.literal: Therefore, observing Ruan Ji's conduct one perceives by what means ritual teaching collapsed; examining Yu Chun and Jia Chong's dispute one sees how chief ministers were mostly perverse; reviewing the merit of pacifying Wu one knows how generals would not yield; reflecting on Guo Qin's plan one awakens to the barbarians' provocation; reading Fu Xuan and Liu Yi's words one finds the wickedness of the hundred officials; checking Fu Xian's memorial and the essay "The God of Money" one sees bribery and favor made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Observe Ruan Ji's conduct and you see why ritual collapsed. Examine the dispute between Yu Chun and Jia Chong and you see how corrupt the chief ministers had become. Review the conquest of Wu and you see how generals refused to yield credit. Reflect on Guo Qin's warning and you see why the barbarians turned hostile. Read Fu Xuan and Liu Yi's remonstrances and you find the corruption of the bureaucracy. Study Fu Xian's memorial and Lu Ji's "The God of Money" and you see how bribery and favor had taken over.

sentences.zh: 民風國勢，既已如此，雖以中庸之才、守文之主治之，猶懼致亂，況我惠帝以放蕩之德臨之哉！

translations.literal: Popular custom and national strength had already come to this; even with middling talent and a ruler who kept to the written order to govern it, one would still fear bringing disorder—how much more when our Emperor Hui ruled it with his dissolute virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Popular morals and the strength of the state had already reached this pass. Even a ruler of moderate ability, content to preserve the existing order, would have feared causing disorder—how much more so when Emperor Hui governed with his dissolute character!

sentences.zh: 懷帝承亂得位，羈以強臣；

translations.literal: Emperor Huai succeeded to the throne amid chaos and was tethered by powerful ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai came to the throne in the midst of chaos and was held captive by powerful ministers.

sentences.zh: 愍帝奔播之後，徒守虛名。

translations.literal: After Emperor Min fled in exile, he merely kept an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Min was driven into exile, he retained only an empty title.

sentences.zh: 天下之勢既去，非命世之雄才，不能復取之矣！

translations.literal: The momentum of All Under Heaven had already departed; unless a hero of the age, no one could recover it!
translations.idiomatic: The momentum of the empire was already lost. Only a hero of the age could have recovered it—and there was none.

sentences.zh: 石勒圍樂平太守韓據於坫城，據請救於劉琨。

translations.literal: Shi Le besieged Leping Governor Han Ju at Dian city; Ju requested rescue from Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le besieged Han Ju, governor of Leping, at Dian city. Ju asked Liu Kun for help.

sentences.zh: 琨新得拓跋猗盧之眾，欲因其銳氣以討勒。

translations.literal: Kun had newly obtained Tuoba Yilu's forces and wished to use their sharp spirit to attack Le.
translations.idiomatic: Kun had just received the forces of Tuoba Yilu and wanted to use their fighting spirit to attack Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 箕澹、衛雄諫曰：「此雖晉民，久淪異域，未習明公之恩信，恐其難用。

translations.literal: Ji Dan and Wei Xiong remonstrated, saying: "Though these are Jin people, long fallen under alien domains, they have not grown accustomed to your grace and trust— I fear they will be hard to use.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dan and Wei Xiong remonstrated, saying, "Though these men are Jin subjects, they have long lived under alien rule and are not yet accustomed to your grace and trust. I fear they will be hard to use.

sentences.zh: 不若且內收鮮卑之餘谷，外抄胡賊之牛羊，閉關守險，務農息兵，待其服化感義，然後用之，則功無不濟矣！」

translations.literal: Better first to gather within the remaining grain of the Xianbei, and raid without for the Hu bandits' cattle and sheep; close the passes and hold the defiles, devote effort to farming and rest the troops, wait until they are moved by your transforming influence and sense of justice, and then employ them—then no achievement will fail!"
translations.idiomatic: Better first to gather the Xianbei's remaining grain at home and raid the barbarian camps for cattle and sheep abroad; hold the passes and strong points, devote yourself to farming and give the army rest; wait until they are won over by your justice and kindness, and then use them. Then you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 琨不從，悉發其眾，命澹帥步騎二萬為前驅，琨屯廣牧，為之聲援。

translations.literal: Kun did not listen; he mobilized the whole force, ordered Dan to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard, and Kun encamped at Guangmu to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Kun would not listen. He mobilized his entire force, ordered Ji Dan to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard, and encamped at Guangmu to support him.

sentences.zh: 石勒聞澹至，將逆擊之。

translations.literal: Shi Le, hearing Dan had arrived, was about to meet and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le learned that Ji Dan had arrived, he prepared to meet and attack him.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「澹士馬精強，其鋒不可當，不若且引兵避之，深溝高壘，以挫其銳，必獲萬全。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Dan's men and horses are elite and strong; his edge cannot be withstood. Better for now to withdraw troops and avoid him, dig deep moats and raise high ramparts to blunt his sharpness—you will surely gain complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Ji Dan's troops and horses are elite; his attack cannot be withstood. Better withdraw for now, dig deep moats and raise high ramparts to blunt his momentum—you will be perfectly safe."

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「澹兵雖眾，遠來疲弊，號令不從，何精強之有！

translations.literal: Le said: "Though Dan's troops are many, coming from afar they are weary and spent; orders are not obeyed—what elite strength is there!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le replied, "Ji Dan's force may be large, but it has come a long way and is exhausted. Orders are not obeyed—where is this elite strength?

sentences.zh: 今寇敵垂至，何可捨去！

translations.literal: Now the enemy bandits are nearly upon us—how can we abandon our position!
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is almost upon us—how can we simply abandon our position?

sentences.zh: 大軍一動，豈易中還！

translations.literal: Once the great army moves, can it easily turn back midway!
translations.idiomatic: Once a great army moves, it cannot easily turn back halfway!

sentences.zh: 若澹乘我之退而逼之，顧逃潰不暇，焉得深溝高壘乎！

translations.literal: If Dan exploits our retreat to press us, we will have no leisure even to flee in rout—how could we dig deep moats and raise high ramparts!
translations.idiomatic: If Ji Dan presses us as we retreat, we will be too busy fleeing to think of moats and ramparts!

sentences.zh: 此自亡之道也。」

translations.literal: This is the way to destroy oneself."
translations.idiomatic: That would be the road to self-destruction."

sentences.zh: 立斬言者。

translations.literal: He immediately beheaded the speaker.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately had the man beheaded.

sentences.zh: 以孔萇為前鋒都督，令三軍：「後出者斬！」

translations.literal: He made Kong Chang vanguard commander and ordered the three armies: "Whoever falls behind will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Kong Chang commander of the vanguard and ordered the three armies, "Whoever falls behind will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 勒據險要，設疑兵於山上，前設二伏，出輕騎與澹戰，陽為不勝而走。

translations.literal: Le held a strategic pass, set decoy troops on the mountains, placed two ambushes ahead, and sent out light cavalry to fight Dan, feigning defeat and fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le held a strategic pass, posted decoy troops on the mountains, laid two ambushes ahead, and sent out light cavalry to engage Ji Dan, feigning defeat and retreat.

sentences.zh: 澹縱兵追之，入伏中。

translations.literal: Dan let his troops pursue and entered the ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dan pursued at full stretch and rode into the ambush.

sentences.zh: 勒前後夾擊澹軍，大破之，獲鎧馬萬計。

translations.literal: Le attacked Dan's army from front and rear, utterly defeated it, and captured armor and horses by the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked Ji Dan's army from front and rear, routed it completely, and captured tens of thousands of suits of armor and horses.

sentences.zh: 澹、雄帥騎千餘奔代郡，韓據棄城走，並土震駭。

translations.literal: Dan and Xiong led more than a thousand horsemen in flight to Dai commandery; Han Ju abandoned the city and fled; Bing province was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dan and Wei Xiong fled with more than a thousand horsemen to Dai commandery. Han Ju abandoned the city and fled. All of Bing province was shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day yimao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month (yimao), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 司空長史李弘以并州降石勒。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Li Hong surrendered Bing province to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong, chief clerk to the Minister of Works, surrendered Bing province to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 劉琨進退失據，不知所為，段匹磾遣信邀之，己未，琨帥眾從飛狐奔薊。

translations.literal: Liu Kun, having lost his footing whether to advance or retreat and not knowing what to do, received a message from Duan Piji inviting him; on jiwei, Kun led his forces from Feihu Pass in flight to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun, unable to decide whether to advance or retreat and at a complete loss, received an invitation from Duan Piji. On the day jiwei, Kun led his forces through Feihu Pass and fled to Ji.

sentences.zh: 匹磾見琨，甚相親重，與之結婚，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Piji, meeting Kun, treated him with great intimacy and esteem, contracted marriage with him, and pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Piji met Liu Kun, he treated him with great warmth and respect, contracted a marriage alliance with him, and pledged brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 勒徙陽曲、樂平民於襄國，置守宰而還。

translations.literal: Le moved the people of Yangqu and Leping to Xiangguo, set governors and magistrates, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le moved the people of Yangqu and Leping to Xiangguo, appointed governors and magistrates, and returned.

sentences.zh: 孔萇攻箕澹於代郡，殺之。

translations.literal: Kong Chang attacked Ji Dan in Dai commandery and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang attacked Ji Dan in Dai commandery and killed him.

sentences.zh: 萇等攻賊帥馬嚴、馮□者，久而不克，司、冀、並、兗流民數萬戶在遼西，迭相招引，民不安業。

translations.literal: Chang and the others attacked the bandit chiefs Ma Yan and Feng Yuezhe for a long time without taking them; tens of thousands of refugee households from Si, Ji, Bing, and Yan provinces were in Liaoxi, calling one another in succession, and the people could not settle to their work.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang and the others besieged the bandit chiefs Ma Yan and Feng Yuezhe for a long time without success. Tens of thousands of refugee households from Si, Ji, Bing, and Yan provinces were gathered in Liaoxi, constantly summoning one another, and the people could not live in peace.

sentences.zh: 勒問計於濮陽侯張賓，賓曰：「嚴、□者本非公之深仇，流民皆有戀本之志，今班師振旅，選良牧守使招懷之，則幽、冀之寇可不日而清，遼西流民將相帥而至矣。」

translations.literal: Le asked plan of Puyang Marquis Zhang Bin; Bin said: "Yan and Yuezhe were never your deep enemies to begin with, and the refugees all have the will to long for home. Now withdraw the army and shake out the ranks; select good governors and magistrates to summon and soothe them—then the bandits of You and Ji can be cleared in no time, and the Liaoxi refugees will come leading one another."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le asked Zhang Bin, Marquis of Puyang, for advice. Bin said, "Ma Yan and Feng Yuezhe were never your bitter enemies to begin with, and the refugees all long to return home. Withdraw the army now, choose good governors and magistrates to summon and reassure them, and the bandits of You and Ji will be cleared in no time. The Liaoxi refugees will then come in one stream after another."

sentences.zh: 勒乃召萇等歸，以武遂令李回為易北督護，兼高陽太守。

translations.literal: Le then recalled Chang and the others, and made Wusui Magistrate Li Hui Northern Protector of Yi and concurrently Governor of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le then recalled Kong Chang and the others and appointed Li Hui, magistrate of Wusui, Northern Protector of Yi and concurrently governor of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 馬嚴士卒素服回威德，多叛嚴歸之，嚴懼而出走，赴水死。

translations.literal: Ma Yan's soldiers had long respected Hui's authority and virtue; many defected from Yan to join him; Yan, in fear, fled and threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yan's soldiers had long respected Li Hui's authority and virtue. Many defected from Yan to join him. Yan, in terror, fled, threw himself into the water, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 馮□者帥其眾降。

translations.literal: Feng Yuezhe led his followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuezhe led his followers in surrender.

sentences.zh: 回徙居易京，流民歸之者相繼於道。

translations.literal: Hui moved his seat to Yijing; refugees returning to him followed one another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui moved his seat to Yijing, and refugees returning to him streamed along the roads.

sentences.zh: 勒喜，封回為弋陽子，增張賓邑千戶，進位前將軍；

translations.literal: Le was pleased; he enfeoffed Hui as Marquis of Yiyang, increased Zhang Bin's fief by a thousand households, and promoted him to General of the Vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le was delighted. He enfeoffed Li Hui as Marquis of Yiyang, increased Zhang Bin's fief by a thousand households, and promoted him to General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 賓固辭不受。

translations.literal: Bin firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 丞相睿聞長安不守，出師露次，躬擐甲冑，移檄四方，刻日北征。

translations.literal: Chancellor Rui, hearing Chang'an was lost, went out with the army and encamped in the open, personally donned armor, issued proclamations to the four quarters, and set a day for the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Sima Rui learned that Chang'an had fallen, he marched out with his army and encamped in the open field. He personally donned armor, issued proclamations to the four quarters, and set a date for a northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 以漕運稽期，丙寅，斬督運令史淳於伯。

translations.literal: Because grain transport was overdue, on bingyin he beheaded Transport Supervisor Clerk Chunyu Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain transport was overdue, on the day bingyin he beheaded Chunyu Bo, clerk to the transport supervisor.

sentences.zh: 刑者以刀拭柱，血逆流上，至柱末二丈餘而下，觀者鹹以為冤。

translations.literal: The executioner wiped his blade on a pillar; blood flowed upward against the stream, reaching more than two zhang from the pillar-top before descending; onlookers all thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: The executioner wiped his blade on a pillar. Blood flowed upward along the pillar to more than two zhang before running down. All who watched believed it a wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 丞相司直劉隗上言：「伯罪不至死，請免從事中郎周莚等官。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Directing Censor Liu Kui submitted a memorial: "Bo's crime did not merit death; I request dismissal of Attendant Gentleman Zhou Yan and others from office."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui, Directing Censor to the Chancellor, submitted a memorial: "Chunyu Bo's offense did not merit death. I request that Attendant Gentleman Zhou Yan and others be dismissed from office."

sentences.zh: 於是右將軍王導等上疏引咎，請解職。

translations.literal: Thereupon Right General Wang Dao and others submitted a memorial accepting blame and requesting resignation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Right General Wang Dao and others submitted memorials accepting blame and requesting to resign.

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「政刑失中，皆吾暗塞所致。」

translations.literal: Rui said: "Government and punishments missed the mean—all caused by my own blindness and obstruction."
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "Failures in government and punishment are all due to my own blindness and obstruction."

sentences.zh: 一無所問。

translations.literal: He questioned no one.
translations.idiomatic: He punished no one.

sentences.zh: 隗性剛訐，當時名士多被彈劾，睿率皆容貸，由是眾怨皆歸之。

translations.literal: Kui's nature was stern and censorious; many famous gentlemen of the time were impeached by him, but Rui generally pardoned them all—wherefore popular resentment all fell on Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui was stern and censorious by nature. Many celebrated gentlemen of the day were impeached by him, but Rui generally pardoned them all. For this reason public resentment fell entirely on Liu Kui.

sentences.zh: 南中郎將王含，敦之兄也，以族強位顯，驕傲自恣，一請參佐及守長至二十許人，多非其才；

translations.literal: Southern General of the Palace Wang Han, elder brother of Dun, by clan strength held a conspicuous position; proud and self-indulgent, with one request he appointed aides and prefectural magistrates to some twenty men, most not suited to their posts;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, Southern General of the Palace and elder brother of Wang Dun, held a conspicuous position through the power of his clan. Proud and self-indulgent, with a single request he appointed aides and prefectural magistrates to some twenty posts, most of them unfit for their duties.

sentences.zh: 隗劾奏含，文致甚苦，事雖被寢，而王氏深忌疾之。

translations.literal: Kui impeached and memorialized Han, wording the charges with extreme severity; though the matter was shelved, the Wang clan deeply resented and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui impeached Wang Han and framed the charges in the harshest terms. Though the case was shelved, the Wang clan deeply resented and hated him.

sentences.zh: 丞相睿以邵續為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Chancellor Rui made Shao Xu Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Rui appointed Shao Xu governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 續女婿廣平劉遐聚眾河、濟之間，睿以遐為平原內史。

translations.literal: Xu's son-in-law Liu Xia of Guangping gathered a host between the Yellow and Ji rivers; Rui made Xia Interior Minister of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son-in-law Liu Xia of Guangping gathered a force between the Yellow and Ji rivers. Rui appointed Xia interior minister of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 托跋普根之子又卒，國人立其從父鬱律。

translations.literal: Tuoba Pugen's son again died; the people of the state installed his father's younger brother Yulü.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Tuoba Pugen died in turn, and the people of the state installed his father's younger brother Yulü.
